title: Fast algorithms and the flopscope billing rules

ideas.title: Exact band entry at flopscope's truncated-SVD rate: re-price the parked k3k construction, not the compression
ideas.mechanism: Lens verdict first. The engine halves the output count M only when it can prove the output is symmetric, either because operands alias (inner(A,A), outer(v,v)) or because an operand is tagged with as_symmetric (_einsum.py / _accumulation/_cost.py: the Cat A/B/C candidates). None of the 23.4% of B spent on legs and D can use this. A leg transport Wt·X is never symmetric. D is needed in full, not just its symmetric part: K21 uses D and D^T with different coefficients, and Yp = d1 D^T d3 + d2 D d2. The polarization trick (XY^T+YX^T from two half-billed Grams) returns only the symmetric part, at the price of one product. float16 bills 1.0, the same as float32. take, compress and 3-argument where all bill at weight 4. So the dominant products already sit at their billing floor. The one rule that does price below the algorithm we use is linalg.svd(M, k=): it bills min(4mnk, economy) for an exact top-k, where the kernel computes the economy SVD and slices. The doc calls this an 'accepted residual'. The construction that sank §54 is exactly a top-r subspace problem. The band basis is the top-r left singular subspace of F = [P·diag(S), A_e, B_e], since F F^T equals the band Gram. After every entry the band Gram in the new coordinates is diag(S^2), so no Cholesky or eigh of M is ever needed. One call svd(F, k=320) returns (1) the new basis P' = U, (2) the entrant's coefficients P'^T A_e and P'^T B_e as column slices of S·Vt, at no extra cost, and (3) the rotation R = P'^T P = S·Vt[:, :r]·diag(S_old)^-1. H stays outside the band as a thin leg. The quantity that changes is the per-entry-layer construction term: k3k's listed ≈4–7u (two Gram applications 2.75u, 2 QR 0.42u, eigh 0.18u, new coefficients 0.63u, rotation ≤1.8u) becomes ≈1.5–1.9u. The accuracy is the already-measured exact top-r arm, not a cheaper approximation.
ideas.cost_estimate: Unit u = one dense n×n×n product = 2n^3 = 0.098% of B plain (0.062% at the 0.636 Strassen billing). Per entry layer: svd(F,k=320) on a 1024×2368 F = 4·1024·2368·320 = 3.10e9 = 1.45u plain. Column scaling P·diag(S) is O(nr). Rotation done lazily is P_cur·R_g at 0.1u per band source per layer (≈4.5u per MLP); done eagerly it is 0.2u per band source per entry (≈9u per MLP). New coefficients and the new M come free. Construction total ≈15–20u per MLP (1.5–2% of B), against k3k's per-entry list of ≈4–7u ×10 entries and the atlas's calibrated lump of 83 bare units (≈8.1% of B). The per-layer band costs do not change: P transport r/n, materialisation P·coef at r/n per band leg, compressed pairing at r/n per band leg, and Z·P^T at r/n, all Strassen-billed. The atlas (2026-09-26_cost-frontier §2.4) has band 6:320 saving ≈100 Strassen units (≈6.2% of B) against 83 bare units, for a net of +2.0 points on the k3l base. Two cases: (a) if all 83 units are entry overhead and it falls to ≈20–35u, the band nets −2.5 to −4 points; (b) if only the listed Gram/QR/eigh/coefficient items (≈4u per entry) are replaceable, the band nets only ≈−0.5 points. Projected util on the k3m base is 21–24.3%, most likely ≈22.5%. Wall: sgesdd on 1024×2416 took 0.39 s on this Mac. Expect ≈1 s on the grader, so ≈+10 s on 61/75 s (mean/max). Residual: one svd call replaces k3k's Gram loop, QR, eigh and Rayleigh–Ritz, so fewer calls. k3k's own residual (0.413 s direct) still has to be re-measured.
ideas.accuracy_risk: Low on accuracy, medium on engineering. The basis is the exact top-r of the band Gram, which is the ideal arm already measured on 10 MLPs: 6:320 costs +1.3% raw, and the q=1 production mirror +1.2%. That was on the k3j base and is not yet measured on k3m with deadcut −2.5 plus the dead-parent column cut being ported now. Two risks. (1) Residual time: k3k read 0.413 s direct against k3j's 0.276 s; materialisation and compressed-pairing calls remain. (2) The rule this leans on. If one prefers not to use the truncated-SVD rate, a randomized 2-pass SVD with oversampling costs ≈3.4u per entry, against k3k's ≈4u, and the idea mostly collapses. So this idea is exactly as good as that billing rule. The 'free' alternative, q=0 with a transported basis and no entry work at all, is NOT a substitute. In my n=512 proxy (MC-derived gating, deadcut −2.5), the transported basis leaves 2.1–2.5% of the entrant's A energy outside, against 0.34–0.5% outside its own top-r (a0=6, r/n=1/4, layers 10–15). The exact entry is the load-bearing part.
ideas.closest_negative: §54 (k3k shared subspace: 'the entry update eats the saving', parked 'only if a cheaper entry update is found'). This is not a new compression and not a re-proposal of the band's accuracy case. The accuracy is measured and unchanged. Only the construction is re-priced, using a documented billing rule that k3k did not use: one exact truncated SVD whose byproducts (S·Vt slices, diag(S^2) as the new Gram) remove the QR, the eigh, the coefficient products and the Cholesky. It is the direct answer to the §54/§58 mechanism ('the construction costs what it saves'): here the construction price itself drops by 2–4×.
ideas.cheap_test: About 10 minutes, no chain run. (1) In a flopscope BudgetContext, call fnp.linalg.svd(F, full_matrices=False, k=320) on a random 1024×2368 float32 F. Check that the billed FLOPs equal 3.10e9 (4mnk) and time it. (2) Run src/estimator_k3k.py on one MLP with the op_log dumped, and sum the FLOPs of its entry block by op to see how much of the 83-unit lump the svd would replace. Stopping rule: if the replaceable share is under ≈30 bare units, or the recomputed atlas util on the k3m base is above 23.3%, the lever is worth less than ×0.94. Stop there. Otherwise run torch shared_sub 6:320 (the ideal arm = exact top-r) on the k3m base, 10 MLPs.
ideas.projected_adjusted: 5.3906e-9 × (util 21.5–23.0 / 24.835) × raw (1.012–1.02) = 5.3906e-9 × (0.876–0.945) ≈ 4.7–5.1e-9 on the grader, most likely ≈4.85e-9 (≈×0.90). In case (b) the result is ≈5.35e-9, i.e. nothing. It does not reach first place: at our raw that needs util ≤≈10.5%, and no billing rule gets there. That has to come from the κ3 state representation, which is the cloud's sufficiency test.

ideas.title: One-sided projection of the old tail's D pairing on a free transported Jacobian basis (legs untouched); proxy says marginal
ideas.mechanism: In D = Σ_s U_s V_s^T, the right factor V_s = [B_s, A_s] is only read. For old sources col(V_s) ⊆ range(J_{l←l−a0}), because A_s = A_e·J_{e←s} and B_s = A_s U_s. The dominant subspace of that product can be tracked for free by P ← qr(Wt·G·P), which is the same subspace iteration the chain already runs on every leg. So D_old ≈ Σ_s U_s (V_s^T P) P^T. Because P is known in advance this costs 2r/n per leg; a data-dependent sketch costs 4r/n, the break-even that closed §55. The legs, t, L1, L2, E and the feed stay exact. Only D_old's row space is truncated. The quantity that changes is the volume of the tail's pairings.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per layer: P transport r/n Strassen-billed, QR ≈2(r/n)^2 u plain, Z·P^T r/n. Per old leg: 2r/n u instead of 1u. At a0=6 the tail pairing is ≈4.3–4.7% of B (atlas: age≥6 costs 10.36% of B on k3l, of which ≈44% is pairings). r=192 (r/n=3/8): saves 25% ≈1.1% of B, minus ≈0.5% basis overhead, so −0.6 to −0.7 points. r=256 (r/n=1/4): saves 50%, minus 0.4%, so ≈−1.9 points. a0=4, r=256: ≈−2.9 points.
ideas.accuracy_risk:
High. Measured here in an n=512 proxy (MC-derived α and gating with deadcut −2.5, B = A·diag(d1)C0 from MC covariance, hub weights φ(α)). Relative Frobenius error of D_old with the transported basis, against the optimal rank-r truncation:
- r/n = 1/4: a0=4 9.5–15% (optimal 2–7%); a0=6 5.0–6.8% (optimal 1.1–2.9%); a0=8 2.5–3.3%.
- r/n = 3/8: a0=4 3.0–5.6%; a0=6 1.0–1.5%; a0=8 0.4–0.5%.
The transported basis is 2–5× worse than optimal, and a top-r SVD of the stacked old A legs is only ≈1.5× better than transported. Against §58's tolerance (1% relative error costs 0.1–1.1% raw; 10% costs ×1.25–1.47), only the configurations that save ≤25% of a small tail are safe.
ideas.closest_negative: §21 (low-rank full D, ×2 worse), §55 (sketching an implicit product breaks even at 4q), §58's note that the old tail's D is rank ≈256 at ×1.008. What differs: only the tail, one-sided, with a basis that costs nothing to construct (2q, not 4q), and every leg stays exact, so t and L1/L2 are untouched. That is unlike §18, §22 and §54, which project the legs themselves.
ideas.cheap_test: Already half-run (the proxy above). The decisive number comes from the real chain: torch chain.py with record=True on MLP 0 at the k3m config. Collect D_old per layer and compute ||D_old(I−PP^T)||_F/||D_old||_F for the transported P and for the optimal top-r, at (a0, r) ∈ {(4,256), (6,256), (6,384)}. That takes one MLP and no extra chain runs. Kill if (6,256) exceeds 1.5%.
ideas.projected_adjusted: Safe regime (a0=6, r=384 at n=1024): −0.7 points, so util ×0.972 × raw ≈1.005 = ×0.977, giving 5.27e-9. That is below grader resolution on its own. The ×0.88 version (a0=4, r=256, −2.9 points) needs a real-chain error ≤1%, where the proxy shows 9.5–15%. Expected value ≈×0.97–1.0.

ideas.title: Symmetric-aware C_pre: the only provably symmetric product in the chain (exact, bundle-only)
ideas.mechanism: C_pre = Wt·C·W, and Wt·W at layer 0, is the only product whose output is symmetric by construction, so it is the only place the symmetric-output rule can legitimately apply. Keep P = Wt·C in the leg stack as now. Then compute P·W only on the block upper triangle, three levels deep: diagonal blocks recurse, off-diagonal blocks go through the existing rectangular Strassen, and the lower blocks are mirror copies billed n^2/4 per level. That saves 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16 = 7/16 of the second product. The engine's own route, a 3-operand einsum('ki,kl,lj->ij', W, C_sym, W) with W aliased, bills the second step at half. But it loses Strassen on the first step: 1.5u against 1.27u now, so it is worse. The quantity that changes is the second C product.
ideas.cost_estimate: Second product ≈0.636u per layer drops to ≈0.36u. The saving is 0.28u × 15 layers ≈4.2u ≈0.41% of B. The cost is 3 extra Strassen invocations per layer (≈60 flopscope calls each, about 20 µs per call), roughly +40–80 ms local residual against k3m's 0.197/0.227 s. That may break the ≤0.2 s local shipping rule.
ideas.accuracy_risk: None: exact up to float32 rounding, and it enforces exact symmetry of C_pre.
ideas.closest_negative: §10/§49/§56 (Strassen engineering is bounded by residual time and wall, not by the meter). This one saves through output structure, not recursion depth. Checked and dropped from the bundle as giving nothing: take→compress (both weight 4); fp16 (rate 1.0); einsum for the pairings (same engine, and 70× slower per §49).
ideas.cheap_test: Bill the block scheme on one layer in a BudgetContext (FLOPs are exact, no MLP needed), and time the 3 extra calls on the Mac. Drop it if the residual cost exceeds 30 ms.
ideas.projected_adjusted: util 24.835% → 24.42%: 5.3906e-9 × 0.983 ≈ 5.30e-9. Below the ≈2–3% grader resolution, so worth shipping only alongside a bigger lever.

verdicts.title: Exact band entry at flopscope's truncated-SVD rate: re-price the parked k3k construction, not the compression
verdicts.already_closed_by: none. §54 parked k3k with an explicit reopen condition, 'worth doing only if a cheaper entry update is found', and this is that update. §58's mechanism (the construction costs what it saves) is answered here because the construction is re-priced from the code, not assumed.
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: Billing checked in source. external/flopscope/src/flopscope/numpy/linalg/_svd.py bills top-k as min(4mnk, economy), which it calls 'the verified randomized-SVD truncated cost'. It computes the economy SVD and slices, so svd(F,k=320) on 1024x2368 = 3.10e9 = 1.45u (1.25u at the first entry, where F = [A_e,B_e] is 1024x2048). Re-priced from src/estimator_k3k.py lines 540-583 at q=1. Per entry the svd replaces 2 QR at 0.21u each (formula 2(2mnk-2k^3/3)), 2 Gram applications at about 1.7u each (A/B 1.375, P part 0.25, H part 0.016*Sb), Qb^T·G·Qb 0.12, eigh(352) 0.18, Pn 0.11, Rb 0.10, Mb 0.06, new coefficients 0.63 and Mnew 0.20. That is about 5.2u per entry (4.4u at e=0) against 1.45u, so delta is about -3.75u per entry and about -37u per MLP, or -3.6 points of B. Costs that do not change and are already inside the measured k3k 27.78%: eager rotation 0.195e u (8.8u per MLP plain, about 5.6u on shared Strassen), P transport about 0.27u per layer, Z·P^T about 0.22u per layer, materialisation and compressed pairings. This lands between the proposer's cases: better than (b), because their 'about 4u replaceable' misses the P and H parts of the Gram and Pn/Rb/Mb; worse than (a), because the rotation, P transport and Z·P^T stay. Applied to the measured k3k (27.78% vs k3j 26.62%, seed 11), band plus svd is about 24.2%, i.e. -2.4 points against k3j. On the k3m base, where deadcut -2.5 trims the band's saving slightly, it is about -1.8 to -2.3 points, so util is about 22.5-23.0%. Raw is +1.3% (ideal arm, 10 MLPs, k3j base) to +2.0% (4 MLPs, k3l base) and is unmeasured on k3m or with the column cut. Adjusted is x0.93-0.96, central x0.945, about 5.1e-9 on its own, or about 4.7e-9 on top of the column cut (4.95e-9). Two cheap extras: move the rotation onto Strassen, and delay the first entry to layer 8, because at e=0-1 the per-entry overhead (about 2-2.5u) still exceeds that layer's saving. Together about -0.3 to -0.5 points. Honest fallback without the svd(k=) rate, a 2-pass randomized SVD at about 3.1u per entry: only about x0.975. Wall: real sgesdd work is about 3.6e10 flops per call, 12x the billed amount. That is 0.39 s local, about 1.2 s on the grader, so +10-12 s, taking the max from 75 to about 87 s of 120.
verdicts.reason: (1) Not closed: §54 names exactly this reopen condition. (2) Allowed. It uses a documented public API at its documented rate, the cost-model doc calls exact top-k at this rate an 'accepted residual', and §5.5 encourages better algorithms. Caveat: about half the gain is purely that pricing gap. Exactness buys no accuracy here (q=1 mirror +1.2% vs exact +1.3%), so disclose it in the write-up, since ARC's reviewers dislike price engineering. (3) The construction is priced, and my re-pricing from the actual code is more favourable than the proposer's case (b). The delta is computed against the measured k3k total, so it does not depend on the unexplained part of the atlas's 83-unit lump. (4) Central x0.945 (range x0.93-0.97) clears 3%, and the util part is deterministic. Three real blockers. First, residual time: k3k measured 0.413 s direct vs 0.276 s for k3j, and the svd removes only about 15 ops per entry (about 3 ms), so the band's own ops (materialisation, compressed pairing, takes) still add about +0.10-0.14 s. That breaks the local 0.2-0.25 s shipping rule, and the grader estimate is about 0.23-0.28 s. Second, the band must be re-ported onto the wide (n x Σw) layout of the column cut now being ported. Third, raw is unmeasured on k3m. Kill test, in order: (a) bill fnp.linalg.svd(F,k=320) in a BudgetContext; it must read 3.10e9. (b) Swap the entry block of k3k for the svd on one MLP. FLOPs must drop by at least 30u and residual must not rise. (c) Run torch shared_sub 6:320 on the k3m base, 10 MLPs; kill if raw exceeds +2.5%. Keep F = [P·diag(S), A_e, B_e, 3H_band] to stay on the measured arm, or keep H exact outside the band.

verdicts.title: One-sided projection of the old tail's D pairing on a free transported Jacobian basis (legs untouched); proxy says marginal
verdicts.already_closed_by: none. No section measured one-sided projection of D_old with legs kept exact. After re-pricing, the §58/§59 mechanism applies (construction ≈ saving), and the accuracy-bearing regimes fail §58's 3-5% tolerance.
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: The per-layer items are right: P transport r/n at Strassen 0.24u at r=384; QR 0.25u by flopscope's 2(2mnk-2k^3/3); Z·P^T 0.375u plain (0.24 on Strassen). But they were counted over about 6 layers, when the basis must be tracked with a QR every layer from early on to converge onto the dominant forward subspace of J (at least 13-15 layers), and Z·P^T is needed at l=6..14. That gives about 9-10u, about 0.9-1.0% of B at r=384, not 0.5%. The saving at r=384 is 25% of the 4.3-4.7% tail pairings, 1.1-1.2% of B, so the net is -0.1 to -0.3 points. Raw at 1.0-1.5% relative error is +0.1-1.7% by §58's tolerance, so the result is about x0.99-1.01. At r=320 (unmeasured, interpolated error about 2.5-3.5%) it is about x0.97-0.995. At a0=6, r=256 the net is about -1.5 points, but the proxy's 5.0-6.8% error means raw x1.06-1.2 by §58, so worse overall. At a0=4, r=256 the error is 9.5-15%, x1.25+, dead. Two more Strassen passes over the old legs per layer plus a QR add about +40-60 ms of residual. Expected about x1.0, i.e. 5.39e-9 unchanged.
verdicts.reason: (1) No section closes it literally. The closest are §21 (full-D low rank), §55 (sketch break-even at 4q) and §58 (tail D rank about 256 at x1.008, but only with the optimal basis). (2) Allowed: exact FLOP accounting, no pricing trick. (3) The construction is under-priced by about 2x. The free transported basis is not free: its transport and QR must run on every layer it is tracked, not only on the about 6 layers where the tail exists. At the only rank that is safe for accuracy (r/n=3/8), that overhead eats essentially all of the 25% pairing saving. This is the project's recurring mechanism again. (4) The best defensible projection is about x0.99-1.0, below the 3% line. The only scenario worth anything, a real-chain error at or below 1.5% at (6,256), contradicts the proposer's own n=512 proxy (5.0-6.8%). If anyone still wants the number, the one-MLP chain.py record=True measurement is cheap, but the prior is strongly negative.

verdicts.title: Symmetric-aware C_pre: the only provably symmetric product in the chain (exact, bundle-only)
verdicts.already_closed_by: none. §10/§49/§56 concern Strassen recursion depth, not output symmetry.
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: The atlas puts the second C_pre product at 0.96% of B (15 bare units at 0.636, layers 0-14; the last layer is diagonal only). Three levels of upper-block-triangle recursion save 7/16 of it, 0.42% of B, so util goes 24.835% -> 24.42%, x0.983, about 5.30e-9. Mirror copies bill about n^2/4 per level (negligible), and Strassen addition overhead on the (m x 1024)(1024 x m) sub-blocks stays about 1%, so the 0.636 billing holds. This is an exact, accuracy-neutral FLOP cut, so unlike accuracy levers it is deterministic and verifiable locally; §60's resolution argument does not apply. It is still below 3%. The unpriced cost is residual time. The off-diagonal blocks of one level can be batched as strided views, but _Strassen sizes its top-level workspace for G=1: X3 at level 0 is (7,1,512,512), so LA = X3[:7G] needs G <= 1. So either enlarged G-batched workspaces (more RSS), or up to 15 invocations per layer (about +0.4 s, fatal). With batching: +3 invocations x about 90 ops x 20 µs x 15 layers, about +80 ms local, taking k3m's 0.197/0.227 s to about 0.28/0.31 s. One level only saves 1/4 (0.24% of B) for about +27 ms.
verdicts.reason: (1) Not closed. (2) Allowed and clean: output symmetry is genuine reduced computation, which §5.5 explicitly encourages. (3) FLOP construction is priced correctly, but the residual cost (+80 ms with 3 levels batched) is the real price and pushes the estimator past the local 0.2-0.25 s shipping rule. (4) x0.983 is a certain gain but under 3%. Ship it only if a bigger lever (for example the svd-priced band or the column cut) leaves residual headroom. Then prefer a 1-2 level version, which saves 0.24-0.36% of B for 1-2 extra invocations.

title: Random-matrix theory, mean-field and free probability

ideas.title: Oseledets (Benettin) band: the shared-subspace tail with a transport-only basis and no Gram/eigh/refinement at entry
ideas.mechanism: Replaces the ENTRY UPDATE of the k3k band (NEGATIVE §54), the one term that made it more expensive than dense. The band legs A_s, B_s are all right-multiples of the same Jacobian product J_{l,m}. By Oseledets for products of random matrices, the dominant left subspace of J_{l,m} is shared by all old m, and it is reached by TRANSPORT ALONE: P_l = W_l^T D1 P_{l-1} (Benettin iteration, rows cut and gated like a leg). A leg that already lies in span(P) stays there exactly, so after entry the coefficients α_s, β_s are fixed. Only the entrant needs a projection. The design keeps P UNnormalised, with only a free diagonal column rescale, so no coefficient rotation (r²n per leg) is needed. The entrant's coefficients come from a least-squares solve against the r×r Gram P^T P. There is no band-Gram application, no Rayleigh–Ritz eigh, and no rotation of 18 legs. QR plus a rotation run only when cond(P^T P) passes a float32 threshold. Materialisation (P α_s), the compressed pairing Z = Σ L1 β^T + L2 α^T followed by Z P^T, and the readout are identical to the validated k3k port. Only the basis update changes. Second arm: a B-only band from a0 = 4 (NEGATIVE §22: B is the tolerant leg, B-only rank 256 at age 4 is far milder than A), with A kept dense, plus the full band from a0 = 6.
ideas.cost_estimate: Anchored on MEASURED k3k (27.78% vs k3j 26.62%), whose entry was about 4–7 plain units/layer: 2.75 Gram, 0.42 QR, 0.18 eigh, ≤1.8 rotation, 0.63 new coefficients, 0.3 P transport. Benettin entry at r = 320, in plain units per band layer: P transport r/n = 0.31, P^T[A_e, B_e] = 2r/n = 0.63, Gram P^T P + r³ solve ≈ 0.1, amortised re-orthonormalisation ≈ 0.1–0.3. Total ≈ 1.1–1.3 plain units per layer, against 4–7 today. That saves ≈ 3–6 units × 10 band layers = 30–60 units = 2.9–5.9 points of B, so k3k-Benettin ≈ 21.9–24.9% against k3j 26.62% (×0.82–0.94). Per band source-layer the cost stays at k3k's measured level (materialisation 2r/n + compressed pairing 2r/n ≈ 1.25 plain, against 4 dense). On the colcut base (≈23.4% modelled), projected util ≈ 19–22%. The B-only arm for ages 4–5 adds ≈ 1 point. If the q = 0 basis needs r ≈ 400 instead of 320, the per-source cost grows by ×1.25 and the low end of the range applies.
ideas.accuracy_risk: The only new error is at entry: span(P_l) = J_{l,l-a0}·span(P_{l-a0}) acts as a q = 0 randomised range finder for the entrant. Halko–Martinsson–Tropp: E||(I−PP^T)A_e||_F² ≤ (1 + k/(r−k−1))·Σ_{j>k} σ_j², so without refinement the effective rank is ≈ 0.7–0.8 r. Measured cliff (2026-09-25_cost §5): 6:256 +7.7%, 6:320 +1.3%. If Benettin at 320 behaves like the optimal 256 (+7.7%), the lever is dead unless r moves to ≈400. Mitigation not yet measured: P already holds the transported dominant directions of earlier entrants, and Oseledets says those coincide with the new entrant's, so capture should beat a random test matrix. Float32 conditioning of an unnormalised P over 10 layers is the second risk.
ideas.closest_negative: §54 (k3k), and the parked 'best case q=0' in 2026-09-25_cost §7. The difference: §54 closed on the COST OF THE ENTRY UPDATE, not on accuracy. The torch ideal arm was +1.3% and q = 1 was +0.2% versus exact. Every variant ever run (ssp with q ≥ 0) applies the band Gram at least once, in the Rayleigh–Ritz step, and rotates the coefficients. This arm removes both, which is exactly the term §54 blamed. It is not §18 (Tucker): there is no core and no truncation of the in-band tensor. It is not §22 (per-source SVD): the basis is shared, needs no per-source range finder, and is built from dynamics, not fitted.
ideas.cheap_test: Torch, 10 baked MLPs, k3m base (deadcut −2.5), through the existing ssp switch. Add q = −1: X = [Wt @ P], no gapply, no eigh, P kept unnormalised, entrant projected by lstsq. Arms: 6:320, 6:384, 5:384, plus the B-only arm 4:256. First number, MLP 0 only, a few minutes: the entrant's captured energy ||PP^T A_e||²/||A_e||² at layers 6–15 against the eigh basis at the same r. If Benettin at r captures less than the eigh basis at 0.8r, stop. Then end-to-end raw. Kill rule: raw > +3% at r ≤ 384. Price the survivors with cost.py (entry term = 1.2 plain), then do the flopscope port on the k3k code by swapping only the entry block.
ideas.projected_adjusted: Baseline 5.3906e-9 (raw 2.1652e-8 × 24.835%). With the colcut being ported (×0.936) and the band at util 19–22% with raw +1.5–3%: 2.1652e-8 × 1.02 × (0.19–0.22) ≈ 4.2–4.9e-9 locally-equivalent, i.e. ×0.78–0.90. The B-only arm on top reaches about 4.0e-9 at best. This does NOT reach first place: it confirms 504aldo's 'shared bases are a 2× lever, never 10×'. It is the only lever under this lens with a measured production anchor and a size above the 2–3% grader resolution.

ideas.title: Chaos (Hermite) ceiling for any O(n²) closure of the old tail — one recorded run decides the whole closure class, and explains §39/§46
ideas.mechanism: Replaces nothing yet. It is a pre-screen with a hard number, and it is not the cloud's slice-fitted block test. Relative to the fresh W_l, which is independent of everything at post layer l−1, the tail readout splits EXACTLY as t_tail,i = K[w_i,w_i,w_i] = 3σ²(W_l^T τ)_i + K^H[w_i,w_i,w_i]. Here σ² = 2/n. τ_c = Σ_a K[a,a,c] is the partial trace, computable from the CP factors in O(nR): for Sym(x⊗y⊗y), τ = (|y|²x + 2(x·y)y)/3. The same split holds for D_ij: a row-constant rank-1 first chaos σ²(W^Tτ)_j plus a (2,1) chaos. Consequence (derived, not yet stated in the notes): the ALL-DISTINCT pass-through has K[a,a,c] ≡ 0, so τ = 0 and it is a PURE third chaos of W_l. That is why §46's amplitude closure of it reaches only R² 0.09–0.39, and why corr(resid_l15, resid_l14) = 0.004. Any O(n²) closure can only reproduce the part of t_tail lying in (i) the first chaos, which is Markov if τ has a cheap recursion (τ_l = d1∘(W^T(G:K)) with G = W D1² W^T, one shared product/layer or its mean-field g0·I), and (ii) the third chaos of a cheap tensor family. The natural family from positive homogeneity is Sym(ν⊗C_post): the matrix is free (C_pre = W^T C W already exists), ν is a vector, t = ν∘var and D = ⅓(ν_j var_i + 2ν_i C0_ij). ν is fitted per source ONCE at graduation and then transported linearly (ν ← W^T D1 ν, O(n²)). This generalises §39's single scalar on μ. The remainder orthogonal to (i)+(ii) is irreducible for the class, and Stage A says the t channel gives no √n discount.
ideas.cost_estimate: The diagnostic is O(nR) + O(n²) per layer on recorded tail factors: seconds at n = 1024, no training. If it came back positive, the production closure for age ≥ a0 costs O(n²) per source-layer for ν transport, O(n²) for readouts from C_pre, and ≈1 plain product/layer for G if mean-field g0·I is not enough. Util would then be ≈ the atlas 'age ≥ a0 free' value + 1–2 points: a0 = 3 → ≈ 9–10%, i.e. the floor.
ideas.accuracy_risk: High, and stated up front. My prior is that the irreducible remainder is ≈ 25–30% of ||t_tail||. §39 found R² 0.92 for μ∘var, which leaves 28% of the norm, against a 3–5% budget at a0 = 4 and ≈1% at a0 = 1. The mechanism: the chain's pass-through maps Sym(ν⊗C) to Sym(D1Wν ⊗ D1 C_pre D1), not to Sym(·⊗C_post), and §59 shows the incoherent remainder consists of near-orthogonal CP terms (κ/√R = 0.5), whose third-chaos readout has no cheap predictor. So most likely this CLOSES the O(n²)-closure class by a principle: 'the non-Markov content is a pure third chaos of each fresh W'. That is itself the write-up's strongest statement, and it predicts the cloud's B2 in advance.
ideas.closest_negative: §39 (amplitude closure, scalar coefficient on μ∘var, R² 0.92, ×17), §46 (all-distinct pass-through vs amplitude, R² 0.09–0.39) and §57 (coherence). It is adjacent to the running cloud test but does not duplicate it. The cloud fits a block to (t, D) and runs the chain. This measures, without fitting, the norm of the component that NO closure in a named family can carry: first chaos plus Sym(ν⊗C) with per-source free ν transported by the Jacobian. Neither the free-ν family nor the chaos split has been measured. It also gives §46 its missing mechanism (τ ≡ 0).
ideas.cheap_test: MLP 0, k3m torch base, record the tail's CP factors (sources of age ≥ a0, a0 ∈ {3, 4, 6}) at layers 8–15. At each layer compute ||t^(1)||, ||t^(3)|| and the best Sym(ν⊗C) fit, with ν fitted at graduation and then transported, not refitted. Report the unexplained fraction ||t_tail − t^(1) − t^(ν)||/||t_tail|| and the same for D. Kill rule: > 5% at a0 = 4 or > 1.5% at a0 = 3 (the Stage A budgets). Only if it passes: run it closed-loop through tailx on 10 MLPs. Hand the number to the cloud session as the predicted ceiling for its Part 2.
ideas.projected_adjusted: If it passed at a0 = 3 (util ≈ 9–10% → multiplier 0.10) with raw +3%: 2.1652e-8 × 1.03 × 0.10 ≈ 2.2e-9 (rank ≈ 4–5). With the measured cost-free accuracy stack (×1.11): ≈ 1.9–2.0e-9 (rank 2–3). If it fails, as I expect, the projected score gain is 0, but the cost axis is closed by a mechanism rather than by five accidents, and the remaining time moves to the write-up and to idea 1.

verdicts.title: Oseledets (Benettin) band: the shared-subspace tail with a transport-only basis and no Gram/eigh/refinement at entry
verdicts.already_closed_by: none (§54 closed k3k on the cost of its entry update and parked exactly this branch: 2026-09-25_cost/RESULTS.md §7 says 'if a cheaper entry update is found (e.g. q=0 validated in torch)'. A Gram-free q=-1 was never run. The B-only sub-arm IS closed by §22.)
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection:
The construction is priced, which is the point of the proposal. P transport r/n, P^T[A_e,B_e] 2r/n and the Gram plus solve come to about 1.2 plain units/layer at r=320. Two items are missing. (a) Z·P^T costs 0.25/layer. (b) The float32 cost of an unnormalised P (flopscope bills float32 at 1.0, so the port runs in float32). In a toy run, cond(P) grows ×1.6-1.8 per layer, reaching 3.5e2 at r=320 and 1e3 at r=384 by layer 15. Solving the normal equations against P^T P (cond 1e5-1e6) is not acceptable in float32. You need a Householder-QR solve every layer (+0.2-0.25 plain), or periodic re-basing, which brings back the r²n-per-leg coefficient rotation, amortised about 0.3-0.5/layer. Realistic entry cost: 1.4-1.8 plain/layer at r=320 and 1.5-2.0 at r=384.

The bigger correction is the rank. I ran a toy in the scratchpad (benettin_toy.py and benettin_toy2.py: n=1024, 16 He-init gated Jacobians, colcut-weighted A legs, band 6:r). The Oseledets premise does not hold at this size. The Lyapunov spectrum has no gap at r≈300. Past about layer 10 the transport-only span captures the entrant WORSE than a plain Gaussian q=0 range finder, because the columns collapse onto the top Lyapunov directions. Whole-band relative squared error at layer 15:
- Benettin-320: 0.0110, against ideal-256 at 0.0118 (ideal-256 was measured at +7.7% raw).
- Benettin-384: 0.0034, against ideal-320 at 0.0032 (ideal-320 was measured at +1.3% raw).
So Benettin at r is roughly the eigh/ideal arm at 0.83r, the edge of the proposer's own stop rule. r=320 should be expected to fail, and the working point is about 6:384.

Re-priced with cost.py on the deadcut -2.5 base (model 24.14%). Scenario A keeps the model's calibration (entry 6.7 plus rotation, per-source saving about 1.75 billed). Scenario B uses §7's itemised per-source saving of about 1.2 billed, i.e. gross ×0.69.
- 6:384 Benettin: util 20.9-22.8%, i.e. ×0.864-0.945. With raw +1.3-1.5%, adjusted ×0.875-0.96 (midpoint about ×0.92).
- 6:320 Benettin (raw about +7.7%): adjusted ×0.88-0.975.
- 6:448: about ×0.915-0.965.

On the colcut-projected base (≈4.95e-9) that gives ≈4.35-4.75e-9, midpoint ≈4.55e-9. On k3m alone it gives ≈4.7-5.2e-9. The proposer's ×0.78-0.90 is too optimistic, and first place and top-5 are out of reach.

The B-only arm at 4:256 is closed by §22. Per-source OPTIMAL rank-256 B-only from age 4 already costs +8.2% raw (4.06e-8 vs 3.75e-8). That is against about 1 point of util (×0.955), so the arm is net harmful, and a shared transport-only basis would be worse still.

Residual time: k3k's direct residual was 0.413 s against 0.276 s for k3j (about 0.23 s on the grader by the measured 2× subprocess ratio). The Benettin variant has fewer ops (no eigh, no QR, no 18 rotations), so residual time is not binding but should be watched on the wide colcut layout.
verdicts.reason: (1) Not closed. §54 closed on entry cost only, and the q=0/no-Gram branch is explicitly parked in 2026-09-25_cost §7. The band itself has a measured accuracy anchor (ideal 6:320 at +1.3%, q=1 at +1.2%), so this is not the §18/§22 truncation class. §62 does not apply: the band REPRESENTS the tensor, it does not close it. (2) Rules: this is a genuine algorithmic reduction, all in flopscope and our own k3k design, so there is no §5.5 or §6 issue. (3) The construction is priced, unlike §54-§59. It misses only Z·P^T and the float32 conditioning cost, both small (+0.3-0.5 plain/layer). (4) The stated mechanism is wrong. The toy shows no Oseledets alignment benefit at n=1024 and depth ≤16: the transported basis is a degraded q=0 range finder, and Benettin at r is roughly the ideal arm at 0.83r. So 6:320 is expected to land near the +7.7% cliff, and the lever lives at r≈384. Even there, the re-priced gain is about 4-12% on the adjusted score (midpoint ~8%). That is above the grader's 2-3% resolution, and it is the only live cost lever of that size besides colcut, but it is nowhere near the top-5 bar. The cheap test is still the right one, with three changes: run at r ∈ {384, 416, 448} rather than 320, include B-leg capture (B = d1·C0 has a flat spectrum, §20), and use a QR-based solve in float32. Drop the B-only arm (§22).

verdicts.title: Chaos (Hermite) ceiling for any O(n²) closure of the old tail — one recorded run decides the whole closure class, and explains §39/§46
verdicts.already_closed_by: §62 ((t, D) is not a sufficient κ₃ state; the cloud result of 2026-09-28), backed by §39 and §46
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection:
0 on the score. §62 already measured the ceiling this diagnostic would produce. The all-distinct part, which the proposal itself shows has τ ≡ 0 and is a pure third chaos, is 28.8% of the next diagonal per layer, and a closure must capture at least 93% of it. The best oracle closer on a cheap basis captured 19.5%. The star ansatz Sym(u⊗C0) alone captured 18.8%. Re-fitting t and D captured 0.16%, because the missing part is orthogonal to both (corr ±0.03).

The proposed family adds nothing to that. The first chaos (τ-driven) lives entirely in the repeated-index t/D terms, which the chain already computes exactly, and it vanishes on the all-distinct part. The Sym(ν⊗C) family with per-source ν collapses to a single vector: all sources share C at a layer, so Σ_s Sym(ν_s⊗C) = Sym((Σ_s ν_s)⊗C). On distinct indices C equals C0. So it is exactly §62's star ansatz, and a ν transported rather than refit can only do worse than §62's oracle-fitted u. The expected unexplained fraction is about 80% of the all-distinct part, against the proposal's own kill rule of ≤5% at a0=4 or ≤1.5% at a0=3. The diagnostic's cost (seconds) is correctly priced but moot, and the production closure (util about 9-10%) cannot be reached.
verdicts.reason: §62 already made the principle-level statement this idea hopes to establish. It ran the test the idea wants to hand to the cloud (star/C0 ansatz, oracle fit, 18.8-19.5% against ≥93% needed, ×25.6 end-to-end for a (t, D) state). It is the recorded cloud result, so there is no longer a prediction to make for 'B2'. The only new content is an interpretation: a Wiener-chaos reading of why the all-distinct pass-through has zero partial trace, which explains §46's R² of 0.09-0.39 and the 0.004 layer-to-layer residual correlation. That is a useful sentence for the write-up's §62 paragraph, but it is not a score lever and not an experiment worth running. Rules and cost are not at issue. It fails at step (1).

title: Algebraic restructuring of the cumulant chain itself

ideas.title: Band entry by projection only: old legs are M_{l,e} times a frozen matrix, so the parked k3k band needs no Gram/RR update
ideas.mechanism: Exact algebra first. Every leg of a source older than a0 is the youngest band member's hub leg times a frozen matrix: A_s(l)=A_e(l)A_s(e), B_s(l)=A_e(l)B_s(e), path X_s(l)=A_s(l)Y_s. There is also an exact identity B_s(l)=A_{s-1}(l)(C_post^{s-1}W_s) - A_s(l)G_s diag(var_s), since C0^s=W_s^T C_post^{s-1} W_s - diag(var_s) and A_s(l)G_sW_s^T=A_{s-1}(l). I checked every exact reordering this allows: Horner over the suffix products, pairing before vs after the transport, building B from neighbouring A legs. Each one still costs 2 transports + 2 pairings per source-layer, because every (l,s) leg is a distinct full-rank matrix read through Hadamard products. So O(L^2) can only be cut by an approximate shared representation, and the one that exists is the band (§54: +1.2-1.3% raw at 6:320). What killed the band was its entry update, which cost about 5.8 plain units per layer (k3k RESULTS §7): 2.75 for two Gram applications on the entrant's dense legs, 0.42 for two QR, 0.18 eigh, 0.2 Mnew, <=1.8 coefficient rotation, 0.63 new coefficients, 0.3 P transport, 0.25 Z P^T. But the old band's span is transport-invariant: a leg in span(P) stays there exactly under X <- W^T G X. So re-selecting the best r-subspace every layer is optional. Proposed update: keep P as the transported basis, project ONLY the entrant (C_e = P^+[A_e, B_e]; the thin H stays exact), and never touch the old coefficients except a lazy re-orthonormalisation every 3 layers (P <- Q, C <- R C). Quantity changed: entry overhead drops from ~5.8 to ~1.3-1.7 units per layer, while the band's gross saving survives (per band source-layer, dense 2 transports + 2 pairings ~1.83 billed become materialisation 2r/n + compressed pairing 2r/n ~0.72 billed). Bonus at the floor: in band form a path leg costs r/n per source-layer (X_s = P(C_s^A Y_s)). So allages (x1.081, 9/10), the one ceiling lever whose cost did not obviously survive a merge, would cost ~3.5% of B instead of ~12.8%. Side result of the same reordering: k4k3 needs 2 dense products per source-layer, not the 4 in chain.py. Contracting over the layer-m row first gives dk4_i = 12 sum_p R2[i,p] (Z^T L_m)[i,p] with Z = W o d2_m o (C0_m D1 W); E_m then follows by linearity. That halves NEGATIVE §61's price, but k4k3 is still unaffordable.
ideas.cost_estimate: Overhead per layer: P transport n x n' x r (0.25 raw, 0.16 with rectangular Strassen) + one QR of P (~0.17) + entrant coefficients Q^T[A_e,B_e] (0.63 raw, 0.40 Strassen) + Z P^T (0.16) + lazy rotation (~0.36 average; 1.07 if done every layer) = ~1.3-1.7 units, against k3k's ~5.8. That is -4.1 to -4.5 units per layer over 10 band layers, ~-4.0 to -4.4% of B relative to k3k. Anchored on the measured k3k (27.78% vs k3j 26.62%), the band's net moves from +1.16 to about -2.9 to -3.2 points. On the k3m base that takes util from 24.84% to ~21.9-22.2% (x0.88-0.895); the calibrated cost model (gross saving 5.5% of B) allows down to ~20.5%. Residual time: k3k added +0.137 s, mostly Gram/RR/eigh calls, and most of those go away; I estimate <= +0.06 s local, which must be measured.
ideas.accuracy_risk: Untested. Without RR the basis tracks the forward-Lyapunov subspace of the OLDEST band source. An entrant at age exactly a0 has its own top-r subspace only partly aligned with it (there is no Lyapunov gap near index 320), so the effective rank can slide toward the §5 cliff (6:256 = +7.7%). The torch mirror's first basis is the entrant's first 320 columns, which is crude; production would use one Gaussian sketch, once. float32 conditioning of the un-normalised P between re-orthonormalisations is a second risk. Break-even is about +12% raw; a clear win needs <= +3%.
ideas.closest_negative: §54 (k3k: 'entry update eats the saving', parked), plus experiments/2026-09-25_cost/RESULTS.md §7, which left 'q=0 (one Gram application)' as the untested best case (-2.9 points). This is the limit beyond it: zero Gram applications, zero eigh, no per-layer rotation. It prices the construction explicitly, which is the §54-59 mechanism: ~1.5 units/layer of construction against ~5.5 units/layer of saving. It re-fits nothing and re-selects nothing (unlike §58's CP refit or §59's sampling), and it is nested by construction.
ideas.cheap_test: No new code: chain.py already contains it. With ssp=(a0,r,q,ov) at q=0, ov=0, X0 = W^T G P and the Rayleigh-Ritz step is a pure rotation inside that span, so only the entrant is projected. Run 10 baked MLPs on the k3m torch config (BASE from 2026-09-29_colcut/pairs.py + deadcut=-2.5, optionally colcut=(-2.5,1e9)). Arms: ssp=None (must print 2.3462e-08); (6,320,1,32) as the k3k reference, expected ~+1.2%; (6,320,0,0); (5,384,0,0); fallback (6,320,0,32), which uses one Gram application. About 1-3 min per arm. Kill if both projection-only arms are > +4% raw; the one-Gram fallback is then worth only ~x0.95. Optional pre-screen: the captured energy ||PP^T X_e||^2/||X_e||^2 of each entrant per layer.
ideas.projected_adjusted: Anchored on k3k: util x0.88-0.895 and raw x1.013-1.03 give adjusted x0.89-0.92, so the grader's 5.39e-9 becomes ~4.8-5.0e-9. The model-optimistic case is ~4.5e-9. Stacked with the dead-column cut (x0.936): ~4.5-4.65e-9. This does not reach first place alone. It is the representation in which the floor-only accuracy stack (allages) becomes affordable.

ideas.title: Consumer-side row cuts: stop producing transport output rows that only feed a dead neuron's own t (use an exact repeated-index surrogate), and D rows whose doubled index is saturated
ideas.mechanism: Every row a product writes has specific consumers. Row i of a transported leg at layer l feeds three things. (a) t_i. (b) D: as the doubled index, every use carries d2_i, d3_i (or w(3,2)=2d2_i), or the DeltaK21 weight d1_i(1-d1_i) - P1_i d2_i; as the single index it carries d1_i or m1_i. (c) The next transport, gated by d1_i. For i dead at the receiving layer (alpha_l < tau), deadcut already removes (b) and (c), but the leg Strassen still produces all n output rows. k3j cut only the inner dimension, because 'the dead rows' own t_i matters, ~4e-9'. Replace that t_i by its exact repeated-index part: t_rep,i = sum_a W^3_ai K3post_a + 3 sum_a W^2_ai (K21post W_l)_{a,i}. K3post and K21post already come out of _nonlin at l-1, and they are exactly what the legs' (3,) and (2,1) slices transport. The only missing piece is the all-distinct pass-through (~23% of |t'|, §46). It reaches P1 through d3_i <= 0.013/sigma^2 (alpha <= -3) and K2 through d2_i <= 0.0044/sigma. Keep the age-1 source's legs in full rows, so its star kappa4 birth and its path readout stay exact on dead rows. Second instance: for a saturated doubled index x (alpha_x > 3), every D-row weight vanishes to leading order: K11 d2_x, paths d2_x, c0d w(3,.)_x, DeltaK21 (1-d1_x^2) = 0.0027. The exception is K22o's term 2(m1_y - P1_y d1_y) D_xy in the kappa4 level scalar u^T K22post u. An exact O(S n^2) matvec restores it: D_{sat,:} c = sum_s L_s[sat,:](X_s^T c). Quantities changed: the M dimension of every non-newest leg and path transport (n -> n_keep(l)) and the row dimension of the D pairing (alive -> alive minus saturated).
ideas.cost_estimate: Needs var_l before the leg stack, so move the fused Wt.C out into its own Strassen call first (0 FLOPs). Saving on leg transports = sum_l legs_l x dead_l(tau), minus the age-1 leg. With the atlas and dead_fractions.json: tau=-3.0 gives ~22.7 raw units, ~14.8 billed (1.45% of B); tau=-2.5 gives ~30.6 raw, ~20 billed (1.95%). Surrogate: one rectangular K21post W_l[:,dead] per layer; sum_l dead_l ~1.5-1.8 raw, ~1.1 billed (0.1%). An optional per-layer amplitude scalar for the missing all-distinct part, fitted on 128 sampled kept rows, costs ~1.9 raw (0.12%). D saturated rows: ~3-5% of 166.5 raw pairing units, ~3.5-5.3 billed (0.35-0.5%). Net ~1.7-2.3 points: util goes from 24.84% to ~22.6-23.1% (x0.91-0.93). Residual time: about +10 calls per layer, ~3 ms.
ideas.accuracy_risk: A dead row's own t is not negligible (WORKLOG 09-24: ~4e-9 if dropped). The surrogate omits the all-distinct part. Its error reaches the final layer two ways: through the mean channel, incoherent via the fresh W; and through K2 via sum_a W^2_ai, which is coherent (§57's 1e-5 parabola). My estimate of the coherent variance shift at tau=-3 is ~1e-6 relative even if the omission is fully same-signed. Estimated cost: +0.3-1.5% raw at tau=-3.0, more at -2.5. The saturated-row D cut is exact to leading order; it leaves the (1-d1^2)D residual and the marg terms.
ideas.closest_negative: Not closed anywhere. k3j's design note says 'do NOT drop the dead rows' own t_i'; this does not drop it but replaces it with its exact repeated-index part, at ~0.1 of a product per layer. The 2026-09-29 dead-column cut works on the producer side (parent columns p at birth). This works on the consumer side (receiving rows i), which is a separate axis, and it acts on the OUTPUT of every transport rather than the inner dimension that deadcut already cut. It is not §57 either: t_rep is an exact term, not a smooth fit. Only the optional scalar is fitted, and it corrects a coherent omission rather than fitting residual noise.
ideas.cheap_test: First number, without changing the chain: run the k3m config with record=True, also storing o['K3'] and o['K21'] per layer. Compute ||t - t_rep||/||t|| on rows with alpha_l < -3 and < -2.5 per layer; expect ~0.2-0.3. Then add a ~20-line read_slices hook to chain.py that overwrites t on rows with alpha_l < tau with t_rep (K21post and K3post of l-1, dead rows and columns zeroed). Arms: t_dead in {exact, t_rep, t_rep + c*mu*var, 0} x tau in {-3.0, -2.5}, plus D[sat,:]=0 with and without the level patch. 10 MLPs, ~1 min per arm. Kill if t_rep at tau=-3.0 costs more than +2% raw.
ideas.projected_adjusted: util x0.91-0.93 and raw x1.003-1.015 give adjusted x0.915-0.94: 5.39e-9 becomes ~4.93-5.07e-9. Stacked with idea 1 and the dead-column cut: 5.39e-9 x ~0.905 x ~0.93 x 0.936 = ~4.2-4.3e-9.

title: Tensor formats beyond CP and Tucker

ideas.title: Slice-exact sliding drop: when a source ages out, its (3,) and (2,1) slices go into the newborn's correction leg (the r = 0, O(n^2) tail format)
ideas.mechanism: Right now a source is carried at 4 products per layer for its whole life, and the window (§16) instead drops it completely, losing its t, D and all-distinct content together. This idea changes one step. At the layer where source s reaches age a0 (after its last full readout), drop s but compute the newborn's correction from what is still carried: dK3 = K3 - d1^3 (t - t_s) and dK21 = K21 - d1_i^2 d1_j (D - D_s) - tree - paths. The post-activation tensor at that layer then has EXACT (3,) and (2,1) slices. The only thing lost is the all-distinct part of G^{x3} X_s at the drop moment. The absorbed slices form the slice-supported tensor Sym(V x I x I). It sits on the newborn's own hub leg A, so it is then TRANSPORTED by the chain's own rule for the newborn's remaining a0 layers (no closure, no fit, no basis), and it regenerates all-distinct content at every later layer. Content older than a0 is re-sliced once every a0 layers. What changes: the per-layer cost of every source of age >= a0 goes to ~0, while t_old and D_old at the drop layer stay exact. For comparison, §58 Stage A shows that dropping them costs x41.8 (t) and x26.5 (D). Nesting: purely additive into the newborn's dK3 (a vector) and dK21. Production: the t part is free. For the D part, D_s must be summed apart from the rest (its pairing is computed anyway: route it to its own accumulator). Fit the FREE alpha-family row by row (beta_i = <D_s^post[i,:], (C0 D1)[i,:]> / ||(C0 D1)[i,:]||^2, then alpha += beta; this is the part already carried free as 3B diag(alpha)). The amplitude-like piece v_j var_i is rank 1. The remainder goes into R ahead of the existing thin range finder.
ideas.cost_estimate: Construction per layer: the t absorption is O(n^2) and the beta fit is O(n^2). Raising the thin rank from 24 to rho = 64 costs a range finder of about 3(rho+8)/n ~ 0.2 units, plus carrying the thin leg at about 3 rho/n ~ 0.19 units per young source-layer. Total overhead is about 0.8 units/layer, which is about 0.6% of B over 12 layers. Sources older than a0 cost 0. Projected util = atlas(a0) x 0.945 (k3l -> k3m scale) + ~0.6%: a0=3 about 8.5% (under the 10% floor), a0=4 about 11.1%, a0=6 about 15.6%, a0=8 about 19.3%.
ideas.accuracy_risk: HIGH, and this is the whole question. k3-chain RESULTS §9 / NEGATIVE §46: the all-distinct pass-through is about 23% of |t'| (0.075 of 0.32 at depth) for the whole kappa3. If aged-out sources feed their next-layer t in that ratio, each re-slicing loses about 20% of the tail's next contribution, which would be x1.3 or worse at a0 = 4. Stage A tolerates only 3-5%. A second, separable risk: at rank 24 the absorbed D can crowd the newborn's own R out of the range finder. The exact-R arm isolates that. My prior that it holds within 3% is about 15-20% at a0 = 6 and under 5% at a0 = 3. The measurement is still decisive either way: it gives, directly, how much of the tail's future content lives in its all-distinct part.
ideas.closest_negative: §16 (window) and §46 (memoryless kappa3). §16 deletes the slices too (J6 x8). Here the slices are exact and then transported. §46 is a0 = 1 (everything re-sliced every layer) with an amplitude CLOSURE standing in for the all-distinct pass-through. Here a0 = 3-8, nothing is closed, and old content is re-sliced only every a0 layers. It is NOT the cloud's B2 either. B2 replaces the tail with a fitted CP block that matches the slices and has arbitrary all-distinct content, and does it one-shot. This is the fit-free, minimum-norm slice-matching replacement (zero all-distinct content), applied per source on a sliding basis. If B2 fails while B4 is fine, this arm tells whether the failure came from the block's spurious all-distinct content (then this passes) or from genuine insufficiency (then this fails too). If B2 passes, this is its production form at O(n^2).
ideas.cheap_test: (1) Open-loop k-step oracle, torch, MLPs 0-2, minutes. At l in {6, 9, 12}, build the post-activation state twice: full, and slice-dropped (a0 in {3, 4, 6, 8}, exact R). Transport both k = 1, 2, 4 layers under the SAME later gatings and births (freeze the rest of the chain). Report ||dt|| / ||t_tail|| and ||dD||_F / ||D_tail||_F. Stop rule: dead if above 10% at a0 = 6, k = 1 (Stage A: 10% ~ x1.25-1.47). (2) Only if it passes: add a slicedrop=a0 switch to run_chain (dK3/dK21 computed against the kept sources, then delete). Run it with corr='free' on 10 MLPs, then split24rr and split64rr. With the switch off, both gates must still read 3.7533e-08 and 2.3135e-08.
ideas.projected_adjusted: Grader raw 2.1652e-8 x (1+delta). a0=3: util ~8.5%, at the floor, so 2.1652e-8 x (1+delta) x 0.10 = 2.17e-9 (1+delta). That is rank ~4 at delta <= 2% (#4-#5 = 2.1-2.2e-9), and 1.5 points of headroom remain to re-buy floor-only accuracy terms. a0=4: 2.1652e-8 x 0.111 = 2.40e-9 (1+delta). a0=6: 2.1652e-8 x 0.156 = 3.38e-9 (1+delta), x0.63 of today's 5.39e-9. a0=8: about 4.2e-9.

ideas.title: Oseledets band: a transported (never re-fitted) shared basis. Each source is projected once at entry, and the projection residual's slices go into the newborn's correction leg
ideas.mechanism: Q (n x r) is initialised once from the first entrant's legs. After that it is only transported (Q <- G W^T Q), with a QR each layer for conditioning. A source reaching age a0 is projected ONCE onto span(Q), after its last full readout. Because W^T maps span(Q) onto span(W^T Q) and gating is diagonal, band legs stay in the band exactly for the rest of the chain: A_s = Q Z_s, with Z_s fixed up to the QR rotation. There is no re-projection, no band-Gram application and no Rayleigh-Ritz, which is the part that cost k3k 4-7 products per entry. Why the basis should be good (Oseledets): the left spectrum of a product concentrates (§6: age 4, top-256 = 97.5%) onto a subspace set by the RECENT matrices, and a long-transported Q converges to the same subspace. The known failure of projections is §22's coherent loss (the discarded A adds up coherently in t). It is removed at entry by absorbing the residual's (3,) and (2,1) post-slices into the newborn's dK3/dK21, exactly as in the slice-exact drop. What changes: cost per band source-layer drops from 4 to 4r/n + 2(r/n)^2. Nested: yes (one projection per source; the span is invariant). This is the r > 0 rung of the same ladder whose r = 0 end is the slice-exact drop, and the fallback if the all-distinct content matters but lives in the fast Lyapunov subspace.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per band source-layer: materialise Q Z_A and Q Z_B (2r/n), compressed pairings L1 Z_B^T and L2 Z_A^T (2r/n), rotation 2(r/n)^2. That is 1.125 units at r = 256, billed ~0.78 (rectangular Strassen, level 2) with alive rows ~0.85, so ~0.75 units, against ~1.88 for a full source at k3m. Per layer: Q transport r/n; QR ~0.13; the final Xi Q^T r/n; entry Q^T[G A_e, G B_e] 2r/n; residual materialisation 2r/n; the projected entrant's pairing 2r/n; D residual into R ~0.3. That comes to about 2.4 units/layer. Totals: (a0, r) = (4, 256) is 107 (young) + 58 (78 band source-layers) + 23 (overhead) ~ 188 units = 18.4%. (3, 256) is 80 + 68 + 25 ~ 17.0%. (6, 320) is about 22%.
ideas.accuracy_risk: Two risks. (a) Entrant capture: at a0 = 3-4 the Oseledets convergence is incomplete, so the entrant may carry more than 1-3% of its energy outside the transported span. (b) The slice fix repairs only the entry layer. The amplitude mode's all-distinct content, roughly Sym(mu x (C - Pi C Pi)), still reads coherently at later layers (the §5 diagonal-aggregation mechanism). That is harmless only if the residual lives in slow Lyapunov directions whose future weight decays, which is unverified. Evidence either way: shared_sub 6:320 = +1.3% despite re-projecting every layer, but 6:256 = +7.7% and 4:384 = +8.7% (a cliff consistent with a coherent, energy-proportional loss, which is exactly what the fix targets).
ideas.closest_negative: §54 (k3k: the entry update ate the saving) and §18/§22 (coherent loss of projections). The differences: (1) no Gram application on band legs at all, so the basis costs r/n + QR instead of 4-7 products; (2) band content is never re-projected, whereas shared_sub and ssp re-project every band leg each layer or entry; (3) the coherent first-order loss is removed by construction at entry, through a structure the chain already carries (the newborn's dK3/dK21). The cost model here prices the construction explicitly (the 2.4 units/layer above), which is the §54-§59 lesson.
ideas.cheap_test: (1) Diagnostic, minutes, one chain pass. Along the chain, measure the capture fraction ||Pi_Q A_e||^2 / ||A_e||^2 (and the same for B_e) with Q transported from its first entry, for (a0, r) in {3, 4, 6} x {128, 256, 384}, against the entrant's own top-r SVD capture. Dead if below 99% at (4, 256). (2) The same k-step open-loop oracle as the slice-exact drop, with r > 0, with and without the slice fix. (3) 10 MLPs, new switch band=(a0, r, slicefix). Run (6, 256), where shared_sub without the fix is +7.7%. Falsified if the fix does not bring it to <= +2%. Then run (4, 256) and (3, 256).
ideas.projected_adjusted: (4, 256) at delta = +2%: 2.1652e-8 x 1.02 x 0.184 = 4.06e-9 (x0.75). (3, 256) at delta = +3%: 2.1652e-8 x 1.03 x 0.170 = 3.79e-9 (x0.70). It does not reach the floor alone, because the band still costs ~0.4 of a full source per layer. It is a real, validatable step (well above the 2-3% grader resolution), not first place.

ideas.title: Feed-form carrier for the amplitude mode: add a fitted vector v_s to the newborn's P2 hub h. This is 'vector x chain-transported D1C0D1', free by construction
ideas.mechanism: The P2 feed is already a nested O(n^2) tensor format in production. It is 3Sym(h x M), with M = D1C0D1 at birth, carried by the chain's own pass-through rule as J M J^T = B diag(d1b) A^T. It is read out as t += 3 m o q and D += 2 diag(m) B diag(d1b) A^T + q m^T, and the first D term rides the existing L2 A^T product. Anything added to h is therefore carried for free, and all additions merge (h stays one vector). Positive homogeneity says an old source's content has an amplitude component Sym(v x C). Its diagonal part is slice-supported (so the slice-exact drop already absorbs it). Its off-diagonal part is exactly 3Sym(v x D1C0D1) to leading order. So when a source ages out, fit a per-neuron v_s and set h_newborn += v_s. Its birth (2,1) slice 2(v d1)_i C0_ij d1_j lies in the free alpha-family, and its t slice is 0 because M_ii = 0. Slices therefore stay exact, and this piece carries the COHERENT part of the all-distinct content that the slice-exact drop throws away. It reads at the next layer as 3 (W^T v)_i (W^T M W)_ii, with the matrix partner carried by the chain's rule. There is no Delta = C_post - G C_pre G drift, which a closure on the current C would have. Use it as the add-on arm between the slice-exact drop (r = 0) and the Oseledets band (r > 0).
ideas.cost_estimate: Carrying: 0 (the existing P2 machinery; h is already a transported vector). Fit per layer, two options. (a) Row least squares of D_s^post against 2 d1_i C0_ij d1_j: O(n^2). (b) The Frobenius-optimal v: the right-hand side A_s(g o diag(B_s^T M B_s)) + 2 B_s(g o diag(A_s^T M B_s)) needs M B_s (1 product); then run CG on (||M||_F^2 I + 2M^2) with M-matvecs, O(n^2) per iteration. That is about 1.1 units/layer, roughly +0-1.1% util on top of the slice-exact drop's figure (a0=3 about 8.5-9.6%, still at the floor).
ideas.accuracy_risk: §46 is the warning: the all-distinct pass-through matches a SCALAR amplitude form with R^2 of only 0.09-0.39. A per-source, per-neuron v fitted to the tensor is a strictly richer n-dimensional family, but it may still capture too little. It only matters if it at least halves the slice-exact drop's error.
ideas.closest_negative: §39 (amplitude closure of the tail: R^2 0.92 on t, x17 end-to-end) and §46. The differences: v is fitted per source and per neuron to the tensor at absorption, then TRANSPORTED (not alpha x the current mu, re-evaluated each layer). The matrix partner is the drop layer's own D1C0D1, carried exactly by the chain's pass-through rule instead of the current C. The slices remain exact through the slice-exact drop, so this carries only the all-distinct remainder and is never asked to reproduce t.
ideas.cheap_test: Inside the slice-exact drop's k-step oracle (no extra harness). (i) Measure the fraction of the dropped source's all-distinct Frobenius norm captured by 3Sym(v x M) (Gram form, as in 2026-09-26_old-tail/stage_b_gram.py). Dead if below 30%. (ii) Measure the reduction of the k = 1, 2, 4 tail errors in t and D against slice-only. Keep only if it is at least 2x at a0 in {3, 4}.
ideas.projected_adjusted: Enabler, not standalone. If it halves the slice-exact drop's delta at a0 = 3: 2.1652e-8 x (1 + delta/2) x 0.10 = 2.17e-9 (1 + delta/2), i.e. the floor at half the accuracy price. At a0 = 4: 2.40e-9 (1 + delta/2).

ideas.title: Block-structured (2,1) slice: skip the D-pairing ROWS of saturated neurons (legs untouched)
ideas.mechanism: D_ij = kappa3[i,i,j], where i is the doubled index. For a saturated neuron (alpha_i > theta), its D row enters the nonlinear step only in three places. (i) Q11, with weight a2_i = d2_i ~ 0, and the c0d and path terms, with d3_i = alpha phi(alpha) / sigma^2. (ii) K21, where d1_i d1_j D_ij cancels against the pass-through subtraction d1_i^2 d1_j D_ij, leaving a residual Phi(1-Phi) - P1 d2 (about -0.04 at 2.5 and -0.012 at 3.0). (iii) K22post, which the closure reads only through the level u^T K22 u. That is an O(n^2) bilinear form per source, ((u o 1_sat)^T L_s)(B_s^T w). This is the row answer to 'rows that carry no information'. Unlike the dead cut, the legs keep those rows, so the saturated content is still transported (identity pass-through). Only the READOUT rows of the pairing are skipped. Measured from experiments/2026-09-27_residual/dump10.npz (10 MLPs x 16 layers, weighted by sources per layer, alive x alive base at deadcut -2.5): the saved share of D-pairing flops is 12.6% (theta = 3.0), 17.4% (2.5) and 23.4% (2.0). The saturated fraction is 18-23% at layer 15.
ideas.cost_estimate: D pairings are about 10.0% of B at k3m (10.62% in the k3l atlas). The saving is 1.26 / 1.74 / 2.34 points of B at theta = 3.0 / 2.5 / 2.0. Construction: row compaction (a gather, O(n^2)) and the O(n^2) bilinear kappa4-level term per source. The rectangular Strassen already exists (k3j). Projected util: 23.6% / 23.1% / 22.5%.
ideas.accuracy_risk: Moderate and threshold-dependent. The neglected weights are the d3-weighted terms in c0d(Q11) and in the path leg Y (about 18% of a kink row at alpha = 2.5, about 5% at 3.0) and the 1-4% K21 residual that lands in R. The covariance channel is hypersensitive (a coherent 1e-4 costs x2.7, §57), so start at theta = 3.0. For comparison, the dead-row cut at -2.5 neglected terms of similar size AND deleted leg content, and cost +1.4% raw. This one deletes no content.
ideas.closest_negative: §48 (carrying only the kink hub columns: ~7% saving, not worth it) and the 2026-09-29 colcut sides result (saturated parent COLUMNS x1.12). Those cut hub COLUMNS at birth, and the saturated ones carry the P2 feed's d1b-weighted matrix B diag(d1b) A^T. This cuts the pairing's OUTPUT rows at the current layer. The feed's D term for the kept rows is unchanged, and the saving is weighted by current-layer saturation, which is largest in the deep layers where the pairings concentrate.
ideas.cheap_test: Torch, 10 MLPs. After read_slices set D[alpha > theta, :] = 0, the transpose-free analogue of the existing deadcut line, but take the kappa4 level from the full D (production computes it as the O(n^2) bilinear form). Sweep theta in {3.0, 2.5, 2.0}. Accept at raw <= +1% (theta = 2.5) or <= +0.5% (theta = 3.0). The gates must be exact with the switch off. The FLOP saving is already measured (12.6 / 17.4 / 23.4% of pairings) and needs no model.
ideas.projected_adjusted: theta = 3.0 at delta = +0.3%: 2.1652e-8 x 1.003 x 0.236 = 5.12e-9 (x0.95). theta = 2.5 at delta = +0.8%: 2.1652e-8 x 1.008 x 0.231 = 5.04e-9 (x0.935). It is multiplicative with the dead-column cut being ported (x0.936), giving about 4.7e-9. This is not a first-place lever. It is a sure, priced one that stacks with the three ideas above, since young-source pairings remain in every one of them.
