verdicts.title: Slice-exact sliding drop: when a source ages out, its (3,) and (2,1) slices go into the newborn's correction leg (the r = 0, O(n^2) tail format)
verdicts.already_closed_by: §62 ((t, D) is not a sufficient kappa3 state; all-distinct part 28.8%/layer, closure must capture >=93%), with §46 (memoryless chain, all-distinct pass-through ~23% of |t'|), §16 and §58 Stage A (tail tolerance 3-5% relative)
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: Cost: the O(n^2) t/beta parts are priced correctly. The D absorption is not. A single aged source's post-D is high rank (the tail D is ~rank 256 at x1.008, §58; §21), so rank-64 R does not keep the slices 'exact'. Exact slices need rank ~256, about +1.7-2.6% of B at a0=3. Splitting D_s out of the sum-of-products Strassen also costs residual time. Accuracy: every re-slicing throws away the tail's all-distinct part. §62 measures that part at 27.2-31.2% of the next diagonal at layers >=8. The band stays that tight while the tail's share of t rises toward 69%, so the tail's own ratio cannot be much lower (inference). That fails the idea's own stop rule (10% at a0=6, k=1) by about 3x, and the 3-5% Stage A tolerance by 6-10x (10% already costs x1.25-1.47). The pure (t,D) state (a0=1) is x25.6. a0=3: util ~8.5-9% (floor), but raw is likely x3-x20 -> adjusted >=6.5e-9, probably 1e-8 or worse. a0=6: util ~16-17%, raw >=x1.5 -> >=5.2e-9. No a0 beats today's 5.39e-9.
verdicts.reason: This is §62's (t,D)-state closure applied to the aged-out tail every a0 layers. The dropped part is exactly the all-distinct content. §62 found it is 28.8% of the next diagonal per layer and orthogonal to the t- and D-terms (corr ±0.03; refitting the coefficients captures 0.16%). The newborn's later transport regenerates all-distinct content for the slice tensor S, not for the dropped remainder E, so that loss is never recovered and it recurs at every re-slicing. The idea's own cheap test (1) is §62's closure.py restricted to the tail, and the number is already known to be ~3x above its kill threshold. The 'exact slices' claim also fails in production at thin rank 64.

verdicts.title: Oseledets band: a transported (never re-fitted) shared basis. Each source is projected once at entry, and the projection residual's slices go into the newborn's correction leg
verdicts.already_closed_by: §54 (shared subspace k3k: ideal 6:256 +7.7%, 4:384 +8.7%), §22 (A-leg projection loses coherently; per-source optimal rank 256 from age 4 gives x1.67), §62 (the slice fix cannot recover the all-distinct part), plus the §6 spectrum numbers
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: The basis, QR, entry projection and materialisation are priced honestly (~2.4 units/layer). The flaw is the rank. By Eckart-Young, no shared basis captures an entrant better than the entrant's own top-r SVD, and §6 puts that at 97.5% for top-256 at age 4. So (4,256) fails the idea's own 99% stop rule by construction; (3,256) fails worse. Passing needs r >= 384. Then a band source-layer costs 4(0.375)+2(0.14) = 1.78 plain units (~1.18 billed) against 1.88 for a full source, and overhead rises to ~3.4 units/layer, so util is ~23-24%, which is no saving. At r=256 the loss without the fix is >= x1.67 (§22, and that uses an optimal per-source basis). The slice fix recovers at most ~71% of only the first-step error (§62). Estimated raw >= x1.2-1.5 -> 2.1652e-8 x 1.2-1.5 x 0.184 = 4.8-6.0e-9, i.e. x0.9-1.1 of today, not reliably a gain.
verdicts.reason: Same shared-subspace mechanism as §54. It drops §54's entry update, and the entry update is what made the basis fit the entrant. Removing it saves construction but gives up the capture. The Oseledets premise is misapplied: the entrant's dominant subspace is set by its last a0 random matrices, which are independent of Q's history (their right singular vectors are Haar-random relative to it). So the transported Q captures the entrant like a zero-power randomized range finder, and that is below the top-r SVD bound, which is itself already below 99%. The discarded A-part adds coherently in t (§22). The entry slice fix leaves the residual's all-distinct content lost (§62: 28.8% per step, orthogonal to anything cheap). The 'D residual into R ~0.3' also assumes a low-rank residual, which is unverified and contradicted by §21/§58.

verdicts.title: Feed-form carrier for the amplitude mode: add a fitted vector v_s to the newborn's P2 hub h. This is 'vector x chain-transported D1C0D1', free by construction
verdicts.already_closed_by: §62 §5a (star ansatz Sym(u x C0) with an oracle per-neuron u captures 18.8% of the all-distinct part, 10.6% at L8 to 26.7% at L14; all five basis vectors 19.5%; >=93% needed), with §46 (amplitude form R^2 0.09-0.39) and §39
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: The carrying cost really is zero: the drop layer equals the newborn's birth layer, so 3Sym(v x D1C0D1) rides the newborn's own B diag(d1b) A^T, and h stays one vector. The Frobenius-optimal fit is ~1.1 units/layer (~+0.1% util). Accuracy: §62's readout-optimal oracle LS on exactly this family (a free n-vector times the C0 partner, pre-gating equivalent of D1C0D1) is an upper bound on what any Frobenius-fitted v achieves on the readout. That bound is 19-27%, below the idea's own kill threshold (30%) and far below the >=50% needed to halve the slice-drop error. So at best it removes ~20-25% of an error that is itself x3-x20 at a0=3 (see the slice-exact drop). Projection: no gain over today at any a0.
verdicts.reason: The mechanism (put the all-distinct remainder into the form Sym(v x C0-like matrix)) is the star closer that §62 already fitted as an oracle and found capturing <=27% even at the deepest layer. Fitting per source and transporting it, instead of refitting per layer, does not enlarge the family on the readout; at one layer all dropped content shares the same M. It is an enabler for the slice-exact drop, which is itself closed, and its dead rule (<30%) is already met by the published number.

verdicts.title: Block-structured (2,1) slice: skip the D-pairing ROWS of saturated neurons (legs untouched)
verdicts.already_closed_by: none (§48-revised / colcut closes saturated COLUMNS, which carry transported content; §2 is Part-I regime pruning and was superseded by the shipped dead-row cut)
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: The saved share is verified. Recomputed from 2026-09-27_residual/dump10.npz (alive x alive at -2.5, weighted by S=l): 12.6% / 17.4% / 23.4% of D-pairing flops at theta = 3.0 / 2.5 / 2.0 (saturated fraction at L15: 18.3 / 23.0 / 27.8%). Construction is O(n^2): the alive-row gather of `left` already exists (only the index set changes), there is a second rmap for the scatter, and the kappa4-level term is a per-source bilinear form. Also needed: `paired_sum` must accept a rectangular m != n output. With D pairings ~10% of B: theta=3.0 gives util ~23.6% (x0.950); at raw +0.3-0.6% that is adjusted ~5.13-5.15e-9 (x0.953-0.956). theta=2.5 gives util ~23.1% (x0.930); raw is more likely +1-2% than +0.8% (the dead-row analogue at -2.5 cost +1.4%, and saturated rows add a K21 residual of -0.04), giving ~5.07-5.12e-9 (x0.94-0.95). theta=2.0: expect a cliff (dead-row analogue at -2.0 = +21.5%; d3 weight 45% of max; K21 residual -0.086), so do not ship. Stacks with the colcut port (4.95e-9) to ~4.7e-9. A 4.5-6% lever, above grader resolution; not a first-place lever.
verdicts.reason: I checked the channel analysis against _nonlin in src/estimator_k3m.py. Row i of D, with i doubled, enters Q11 and the c0d/path/marg terms only with the saturated neuron's own d2_i or d3_i. It enters K21 with coefficient Phi_i d1_j minus P1_i d2_i d1_j. After the pass-through subtraction d1_i^2 d1_j that leaves (Phi(1-Phi) - P1 d2) d1_j = -0.012 / -0.038 at alpha 3.0 / 2.5, and that remainder lands in a thin R that already truncates to rank 24. The legs and transported content are untouched, so the colcut failure mode (saturated columns carry pass-through content) does not apply. Corrections to the cheap test: (1) K22o's only O(1)-weight D-terms for saturated rows are separable, 2 Phi_i (m1_j - P1_j d1_j) D_ij u_i u_j, so the bilinear trick works for those. The C0-elementwise pieces (-2 Q11^2 cross term, c0d with w(3,2) = 2 d2) cannot be recovered without the skipped rows. They are d2_i-weighted and must simply be dropped, so the torch arm must mimic that, not 'take the level from the full D'. The level is compounding-sensitive (§52: 5% -> x2.8). (2) Measure on 10 MLPs on both the k3m base and the matched colcut -2.25 base, which is what ships next. Accept theta=3.0 at raw <= +1%.

title: Statistics, sketching and hybrid estimators

ideas.title: Saturated-ROW readout cut of the D pairings, with the kappa4 level restored exactly in O(n^2). The saturated-side counterpart of the dead-row cut, applied to the readout only
ideas.mechanism: Quantity changed: the rows i of the D-pairing output D = sum_s [L1_s B_s^T + L2_s A_s^T] (plus the path and feed terms that ride on it) for neurons that are saturated at the current layer (alpha_i = mu_i/sigma_i > a_sat). Only the left-factor rows are cut. Leg rows, D columns and t_i are all kept. Why the rows carry almost no information: a saturated neuron is close to identity, so the pass-through legs already carry kappa3[i,i,j] exactly. I went through every consumer of D_ij in nonlin_slices, _nonlin and the birth code and wrote down the weight each one puts on row i. Every weight decays with alpha: (a) Q11 (the covariance) has 0.5*d2_i*d1_j, so phi(alpha); (b) the C0*D term in Q11 has w31_i, so alpha*phi; (c) dK21 = K21 - d1^2 d1 D - tree has D_ij*d1_j*[d1_i(1-d1_i) - P1_i d2_i], also about alpha*phi. In K21 the O(1) part d1_i d1_j D_ij cancels exactly against the pass-through subtraction. (d) The path births Y enter through d2_x and d3_p. (e) K3 minus d1^3 t cancels. The one consumer with an O(1) weight is the post-kappa4 (2,2) slice: K22o[i,j] contains [d1_i*alpha_j - 2(P1 d2)_i (P1 d1)_j] D_ij. It enters the chain only through the scalar level (Ssum, trM). A level shift compounds (k4mult 1.05 costs x2.8), so this term must be restored. It can be restored exactly with two matvecs of the cut row block: D_sat*(u.alpha) and D_sat*(u.P1.d1), with u = rowsum(W_{l+1}^2). Each is L1_s[sat](B_s^T x) + L2_s[sat](A_s^T x) per source. Row weights relative to a kink neuron (dK21 weight 0.091 at alpha=0, |w31| max 0.24, d2 max 0.40): at alpha = 3.0 they are 0.012, 0.013 and 0.0044; at 3.5 they are 0.003, 0.003 and 0.0009; at 2.5 they are already 0.038, 0.044 and 0.0175. The dK21 weight decays slowly because P1*d2 ~ alpha*phi(alpha), so the natural threshold is a_sat about 3.0 to 3.5, not 2.5. Measured on dump10.npz (10 MLPs, per-layer alpha): the saturated fraction per layer equals the dead fraction (sign symmetry of the columns of W), reaching 18% (alpha > 3) and 23% (alpha > 2.5) at layer 15.
ideas.cost_estimate: Construction: zero. The mask comes from mu_pre and var, which exist before the pairing, and the rectangular Strassen with row compaction and rmap scatter already exists from k3j. The level fix costs about 8*S*n^2 flops per layer, about 0.06 dense units, which is negligible. Residual time: two extra take ops per layer. Saving: the D pairings are about 9.7% of B at k3m (atlas 10.62% at k3l, scaled by sum_l l(1-f)^2 = 76.0/83.3). The cost-weighted share of their rows that is cut, computed from dump10.npz with weight l*(1-f_dead) per layer: 8.9% at alpha > 3.5, 12.6% at > 3.0, 17.4% at > 2.5. That is -0.86, -1.22 and -1.68 points of B, giving util 24.84% -> 23.97%, 23.61% or 23.15% (x0.965, x0.951, x0.932), multiplicative with the column-cut port. This is a model: the D-pairing cost scales with rows x cols, as the dead-row cut measured.
ideas.accuracy_risk: Moderate at 3.0 and low at 3.5. The neglected terms have the same order as those the dead-row cut at -2.5 already neglects (Phi(-2.5) = 0.006, phi = 0.0175), except the dK21 row weight alpha*phi, which is 0.012 at 3.0. Row i of dK21 becomes the E column of hub i in the new source. Today's colcut run showed that saturated E columns matter (x1.12 when they are zeroed at alpha > 3). Here only the part proportional to D_ij (row i) changes. The main content of those columns is the C0*D term d1_i w31_j D_ji C0_ij, which uses column i of D (row j) and is kept. My rough estimate is that the perturbed share is at most about a third of that content, i.e. x1.00 to x1.04 raw at 3.0. Without the level fix a systematic level bias is possible. This is a structural lever of about 4 to 5%, just above the grader's resolution. Its expected value for the private re-evaluation should be judged on the local 100-MLP paired test, not on the public 50-MLP grade.
ideas.closest_negative: NEGATIVE §48 and experiments/2026-09-29_colcut. Cutting saturated birth COLUMNS costs x1.12 at alpha > 3 because saturated hubs carry transported content (the thin ER / C0*D part). This idea cuts the other axis, the saturated READOUT ROWS of D, and keeps the legs and the columns. The Wick-coefficient algebra shows that row i of D enters every consumer at O(Phi(-alpha), alpha*phi(alpha)) except a scalar, which is restored exactly. It is also not the dead-row cut (k3j/k3m): that cut gates the legs to 0 and drops rows from the transport, whereas saturated leg rows must be transported and stay untouched here.
ideas.cheap_test: chain.py, torch, 10 baked MLPs, about 2 minutes per arm on the Mac. After read_slices and the deadcut masking, set sat = (mu_pre/sqrt(var)) > a_sat and D[sat, :] = 0 (rows only). Arm (b) also computes the kappa4 level from a K22o built with the uncut D, which emulates the O(n^2) fix; everything else sees the cut D. Grid a_sat in {3.5, 3.0, 2.5} x {no fix, fix}, on the k3m base (2.3462e-8) and on the matched column-cut base at -2.25. Self-check: a_sat = 1e9 must reproduce the base bit for bit. Kill criterion: raw worse than +1.0% at a_sat = 3.0 with the fix, or worse on 6 or more of 10 MLPs. If it passes, measure util in flopscope before claiming the saving.
ideas.projected_adjusted: At a_sat = 3.0 with the fix and raw +0.3%: x0.951 x 1.003 = x0.954, so 5.3906e-9 -> about 5.14e-9 on the grader alone. Stacked on the column-cut port at -2.25 (projected 4.95e-9): about 4.72e-9. At 3.5: x0.967 -> about 4.79e-9 stacked. Honest scope: a structural step of 3 to 5%. It does not bring first place (which needs util about 10.5% at raw 1.62e-8).

ideas.title: Saturated-HUB half-column cut: drop only the B column and the L1*B^T pairing column of saturated parents, keep A and the thin ER (a mechanistic refinement of today's colcut finding)
ideas.mechanism: Quantity changed: the columns p of the tree leg B_s, and the matching inner columns of the L1*B^T pairing, for parents with alpha_p > a_sat at birth. The A_s columns, ER (H*Ut) and dK3 are kept. Today's colcut run found that zeroing saturated columns costs x1.12. The same Wick algebra as in the first idea says what those columns carry. It is ER column p, which is row p of the thin R and holds the non-cancelling C0*D term d1_p w31_j D_jp C0_pj, and it is read through A_p. Every weight on B_p vanishes. The tree weight g_p = phi(alpha)/sigma is 1.1% of kink at alpha = 3 and 4.4% at 2.5. The E-leg term 3*B*alpha has alpha_p about 2*alpha*sigma*Phi(-alpha), i.e. 0.008 sigma (2% of kink) at 3 and 0.031 sigma (7.8%) at 2.5. The feed hub h_p is proportional to d2_p, and the path-leg column X_p to d3_p and d2_p. So L1_p = 2A g B + A^2 alpha is about 0, and the L1*B^T pairing loses column p at no cost. L2_p = (2/3)(E.A) + ... keeps its ER.A part, so the L2*A^T pairing and the A transport keep column p. The one exception is the P2 feed: q = rowsum(B.d1b.A) and 2 diag(m) B diag(d1b) A^T have d1b_p close to 1, so the feed's M = D1 C0 D1 does not decay on the saturated side.
ideas.cost_estimate: Construction: zero. It needs per-leg column widths, which is exactly the wide (n x sum of widths) layout the dead-column-cut port must build anyway, so no extra engineering. Saving: lifetime-weighted saturated columns (colcut table, same as the dead side by symmetry) are 4.1% at alpha > 3.0 and 6.4% at > 2.5. They multiply the B transports (about 5.95% of B at k3m) plus the L1*B^T half of the pairings (about 4.85%): -0.44 points (x0.982) or -0.69 points (x0.972). Modelled, not measured.
ideas.accuracy_risk: The main risk is the P2 feed, which loses about 4 to 6% of its M columns. The feed alone is worth x1.03, and x1.125 together with marg and K31, so a loss of about x1.003 to x1.01 is plausible. Secondary losses are g*B^2 and 3*B*alpha at 2 to 8% of kink weight on 4 to 6% of columns. If the premise is wrong (the x1.12 lives in B rather than in ER), this arm will show about x1.1 immediately.
ideas.closest_negative: 2026-09-29_colcut, sides.py, saturated side (x1.1234 at alpha > 3, x1.39 at > 2.5). That arm zeroed B, ER, B2, dK3, alpha, g, d3, d1b, h and g3 together. This arm keeps ER, dK3 and A. It tests whether the saturated content is the thin E part (predicted) or the B leg. It is not §48's d2-mass proxy either: the proxy is replaced by the actual per-consumer weights.
ideas.cheap_test: chain.py, 10 MLPs, one switch mirroring colcut. For hubs with alpha_p > a_sat, zero src B[:,p], B2[:,p], g_p, alpha_p, h_p, g3_p, d3_p and d1b_p, but NOT ER[:,p] or dK3_p. Run a_sat in {3.0, 2.5}. Add a diagnostic arm that also keeps B_p inside the feed only, to measure the feed's share. Kill if raw is worse than +1% at 3.0. Run it only after the first idea, because both share the port.
ideas.projected_adjusted: Alone: x0.972 to 0.982 on util, times about x1.005 raw, gives about x0.98 to 0.99, which is at or below the grader's resolution. Together with the first idea and the column cut: about 4.6e-9 to 4.7e-9. It does not bring first place. Its main value is a clean mechanistic statement for the write-up (the value of a saturated column is its thin correction content, not its tree leg) at zero extra engineering.

ideas.title: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT HERE, do not pursue: sampling or sketching the old tail in the readout norm (t, D) instead of the tensor norm, and the MC or Hutchinson hybrids around it
ideas.mechanism: The brief's premise: sample birth columns (CP terms) with Horvitz-Thompson reweighting, with the error governed by the readout. The chain reads the tail only through t_old(l) and D_old(l); I checked read_slices, so this part is correct. The relevant constants are therefore kappa_t = sum_c ||t_c|| / ||t|| and kappa_D = sum_c ||D_c||_F / ||D||_F, not §59's tensor kappa. Measured with a tree-only k=3 chain on Gaussian-closure moments, in the scratchpad (kappa_readout.py, n = 256 and 512, L = 12, a0 in {1, 4}, 2 seeds): kappa_T/sqrt(R) = 0.47 to 0.58, which reproduces §59's 0.50 at n = 1024, so the synthetic chain is faithful on this metric. kappa_D = 0.85 to 0.95 of kappa_T and kappa_t = 0.78 to 0.92 of kappa_T: at n = 512, kappa_D = 31 to 39 and kappa_t = 26 to 37. The sum IS coherent: D_old's top singular value holds 33 to 66% of its energy and cos(D_old, var mu^T) = 0.45 to 0.68, so the rigorous lower bound kappa_D >= ||D||/sqrt(sigma1^2 + sigma2^2 + sigma3^2) (each column's D-slice has rank at most 3) is only 1.1 to 1.45. The TERMS, however, are nearly orthogonal to it. Coherence of the sum is not coherence of the terms. Projected at n = 1024: kappa_D about 0.9 x 62, about 55, i.e. about 170% error at r = n.
ideas.cost_estimate: Would have been 5.85% of B at a0 = 1 and r = n, 12.69% at a0 = 4 (§59 cost_merge). But a bound independent of any measurement closes the floor anyway. kappa >= 1 always, and the a0 <= 2 tolerance is about 1 to 1.5% (§59 Stage A), so any unbiased sampler with r <= 2n columns has error >= 1/sqrt(2n) = 2.2%, above the tolerance even with perfect coherence. The 10% floor is therefore unreachable by unbiased column sampling in any norm.
ideas.accuracy_risk: Dominated variants: (1) a skewed-probe sketch (E z^3 = 1, u = A(g.z), v = Bz, which folds all sources into rank k) has per-probe variance ||A_i g||^2 ||B_i||^4, worse than column importance sampling by about sqrt(R). (2) Random-projection AMM of the D-pairing inner dimension has error ||X||_F ||Y||_F / sqrt(k), which is at least the importance-sampling error, and it still needs the legs materialised. (3) Hutchinson or Hutch++ has no target: every diagonal the chain reads comes together with a full matrix it also needs. Where only a diagonal is needed (var at the last layer) it already costs one product, and the per-probe relative variance there is about ||offdiag row||^2 / diag^2, about 16 at participation ratio 65. (4) An MC blend: 6.5k samples give MSE about 1.2e-5 against the chain's 2.2e-8, so the optimal inverse-variance blend gains at most 0.2%. (5) Importance sampling of the transport's contraction index (hidden units): the all-distinct sum is incoherent, so the relative error is about 3*sqrt((1-pi)/pi).
ideas.closest_negative: §59 (tensor-norm kappa = 62). This closes the one opening §59 left, the readout norm, and adds the kappa >= 1 floor bound. It is also consistent with §62: the part the readout needs is orthogonal to every cheap direction, and here it is orthogonal at the level of individual terms too.
ideas.cheap_test: Confirm at n = 1024 in about 10 minutes. On MLP 0, torch chain k3m config with tailx a0 in {1, 4}, at layers 11, 13 and 15: compute per-column ||t_c|| and ||D_c||_F in O(nR), including the E and ER terms, plus ||D_old||_F. Expect kappa_D in the 45 to 60 range. If kappa_D < 3 appears anywhere, the synthetic prior was wrong and the question reopens only for a0 = 3 to 4. My scratch script is <scratchpad>/kappa_readout.py.
ideas.projected_adjusted: None. Even the best case (kappa <= 1.5 at a0 = 3 to 4, r = n to 2n) would only reach util 11 to 14% and about 2.6e-9 to 2.9e-9, and the measured kappa is 20 to 40 times too large. Verdict for this lens: no statistical or sketching route reaches first place. Unbiased estimators of the tail's readout inherit the terms' orthogonality, and the only lens-derived gains are the small saturated-side cuts above.

verdicts.title: Saturated-ROW readout cut of the D pairings, with the kappa4 level restored exactly in O(n^2)
verdicts.already_closed_by: none
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection: Cost numbers checked against dump10.npz. The D pairing runs at layers 1-14 with S = l sources, and the cost-weighted saturated row share is exactly the claimed 8.9% / 12.6% / 17.4% at a > 3.5 / 3.0 / 2.5 (12.9% on the -2.25 dead base). Construction is genuinely free in estimator_k3m.py: (1) alive_cut already computes a = mu_pre/sqrt(var) before the pairing; (2) GLv is already a take over the left stack, so only the index array changes; (3) _rec_sum already accepts m != p. The level fix costs about 0.1% of B and about 5 extra ops per layer. Two small corrections to the saving. The right-operand Strassen combos do not shrink, so the saving is about 0.97 of the modelled figure: -1.19 points, util x0.952 at 3.0 and x0.966 at 3.5. Raw is a prior, not a measurement: +0.3 to +1.5% at 3.0 and +0 to +0.5% at 3.5. That gives adjusted x0.955-0.967 at 3.0 and x0.966-0.971 at 3.5, so 5.39e-9 -> about 5.15-5.23e-9 alone and about 4.73-4.80e-9 on top of the column-cut port. The gain is 3-4.5%, just above the grader's resolution. It does not change the first-place arithmetic.
verdicts.reason: Not closed. No section tests saturated D rows: §48-revised and colcut cut columns, deadcut is the dead side, and §19/§21 truncate D by age or rank. It is also allowed, since skipping products whose rows the nonlinear step barely reads is a real cut in computation, the same kind as deadcut. I checked the consumer list against production _nonlin and it is complete. Row i reaches Q11 only through cf21_i and d3_i, reaches the paths through d2_i and d3_i, and reaches K22o only through the scalar Ssum. The two-vector fix (a*u and P1*cf11*u on the j side) restores the factorizable part of Ssum; the parts it leaves out are the c0d and Q11^2 terms, which carry d2_i weights. Three corrections to the stated mechanism change the risk, not the verdict. (1) With marg=True (shipped), the cancellation in K21 is NOT exact. K21 carries 0.5*cf22_i*cf11_j*D_ij, while the pass-through subtracts d1_i^2*d1_j*D_ij, which leaves a non-decaying d1_i*delta_j*D_ij with delta_j = d4 t/6 + d5 K4d/24. Measured on dump10, its rms is about 3-5% of the kink-row weight 0.091*d1_j at layers 8-14. So the lost weight floors at roughly 5-7% of kink at a = 3.5, not 3%, and a = 3.5 is not 'low risk'. (2) With paths on, the C0*D term in a saturated R row is subtracted by the path birth (Yp*B), so it carries the same small factor. It is not the 'main content' of saturated E columns. That content is the O(1) kappa4 Wick term 0.5*cf22_i*cf21_j*K22_ij, which the cut keeps, and this supports the accuracy prior. (3) The risk that needs watching is coherent: [d1(1-d1) - P1 d2] is negative for every saturated hub, and E enters t with A^2 >= 0 weights (§22). The covariance channel at a > 3 (d2_i about 1.1% of kink on about 15% of deep rows) is the same order as the -3 -> -2.5 dead band, which cost about +1.4% raw in total. So +1% at 3.0 is a realistic outcome. That argues for running {3.0, 3.25, 3.5}, fix arms only, with the idea's kill rule (> +1.0% raw, or worse on >= 6/10). Also note that the emulated fix (uncut K22o) restores slightly more than the production fix does, which is negligible at a >= 3.

title: Learned closures and surrogates within the rules

ideas.title: Slice-Markov tail (MST): keep the young sources exact and carry the old tail only as its own (t, D), moved forward by the exact repeated-index rule. This is the best closure any (t, D, C, kappa4) state can give, and it is a one-step test of every learned kappa3 closure
ideas.mechanism: Sources younger than a0 stay exact. When a source reaches age a0, its post-gated slices are added to a tail state (tau, Delta). The slices are t~_s = d1^3 t_s and D~_s,ij = d1_i^2 d1_j D_s,ij. The readout computes them already, so graduation is free, and because the state is linear in the tensor it is nested by construction. That is the reverse of the failure behind 54/55/58/59. At each layer: t'_i = sum_a W_ai^3 tau~_a + 3 sum_a W_ai^2 (Delta~ W)_ai and D' = (W∘W)^T (diag(tau~) W + Delta~ W) + 2 (W∘(Delta~ W))^T W, with the diagonal zeroed. This is exact for every tensor entry that has a repeated index. The only thing dropped is the all-distinct pass-through sum_{abc distinct} W_ai W_bi W_ci K_abc. Why a learned closure cannot recover it: W_{l+1} is independent of K_l, so given ANY O(n^2) state this term has conditional mean zero. The one exception is K's projection onto tensors built from the state, Sym(x⊗M) with x in {mu, t} and M in {C, D_sym}. The rest has per-neuron RMS sqrt(6(2/n)^3)·||K_ad||_F and is uncorrelated with every feature, and 59 measured that Frobenius mass as nearly orthogonal (kappa/sqrt(R)=0.5). So the injector is the runtime-levelled amplitude pattern only: level ≈ v/2 per k3-chain RESULTS §9, no fitted constant, built from var' and W^T mu~ that we already have. That answers the lens question. A learned closure transfers only for content whose conditional mean given the state is nonzero: W-even, self-averaging content, which is why K4d = 3 v var^2 works. It also explains why 44 and 57 found only incoherent residuals. MST plus the injector is therefore the conditional-mean slice closure, and its number is a lower bound on the error of the cloud's B2 and of every learned (t, D, C, kappa4) closure, obtained without any fitting.
ideas.cost_estimate: The whole tail costs 3 dense n^3 products per layer: Delta~W, then (W∘W)^T[...], then (W∘Delta~W)^T W. The last layer needs 1 (t' only). For a0=3 that is about 37 products × 0.636 ≈ 23.5 units ≈ 2.3% of B. The injector is O(n^2). Construction cost is zero, because the graduating slices already exist. Totals: a0=3 gives 8.32% (atlas) + 2.3% ≈ 10.6%. a0=4 gives ≈13.4%. A partial variant retires only births 0–2 at age 3; it saves ≈132−36 = 96 products ≈ 6% of B, for util ≈18.8%.
ideas.accuracy_risk: HIGH. I expect it to fail and give it P(success) ≈ 5–10%. For the whole tensor, the all-distinct pass-through is 23% of |t'| (MC, k3-chain RESULTS §9: 0.075 of 0.32 at layer 13). I applied the fresh-W variance formula to 59's ||T|| (with the factor 3 of Sym(B⊗3A⊗B) and d1 gating). It gives the same order, and the tail holds most of that Frobenius mass. So I expect f_tail ≈ 0.15–0.3 per step. The injector explains R² ≤ 0.39, so it cuts f by at most ≈22%. My error model (Stage A quadratic: t ×(1+25δ²), D ×(1+60δ²); steady-state δ ≈ tail share × 1.7f) puts break-even for full retirement at a0=3 near f ≈ 0.08. The design already satisfies the generalisation conditions: (1) it learns no per-neuron pattern, only runtime-levelled patterns; (2) any coefficient must pass a spread test (fit per MLP on 10 MLPs, spread < 10% of the mean, then held-out closed loop); (3) the closure is run in closed loop from the start, which avoids the iterated-operator divergence in 15; (4) the effect is structural (≥5%, needed 10/10), so 60 does not apply.
ideas.closest_negative: The closest is 46, a memoryless kappa3 chain with an amplitude closure. It was closed by a one-step extrapolation ("~18% t error") and never run end-to-end, and it made the YOUNG content memoryless too. Next is 39, which replaced the tail's slices by an amplitude fit and carried none of the tail's own slices. MST keeps the young sources exact, carries the tail's exact slices, and transports every repeated-index entry exactly. It also differs from the cloud's B2: there is no fitted block, so no spurious all-distinct content and none of 58's fitting cost. It is the minimum-norm slice-consistent tensor, i.e. the conditional-mean closure. It is not a representation of the tensor, so 54/55/58/59 do not apply.
ideas.cheap_test: Run on MLP 0 in torch at n=1024 with the k3m config and tailx-style separate accumulation at a0=3 and a0=4. At layers 6, 9, 12 and 14, apply the repeated-index transport to the tail's post-gated slices and compare with the exact slices of the SAME source set at l+1 (read from the legs). Report f_t = ||t_exact − t_MST||/||t_exact||, and f_D likewise, split by birth layer. Also report the R² of the residual on the runtime amplitude pattern. Self-checks: MST plus the all-distinct part from the legs (full minus repeated, by inclusion–exclusion) must reproduce the exact slices to 1e-12, and a0 > L must be bitwise base. This takes minutes. Stop if f_t or f_D > 0.08 at any layer ≥ 9. Also check that the residual RMS matches sqrt(6(2/n)^3)·||K_ad,tail|| from stage_b_gram.norm2_T. If it matches, write the parity principle into the write-up: it explains 16, 39, 44, 46, 57 and 59, and predicts B2 ≫ base while B4 ≈ base. Only if f ≤ 0.08: run closed loop on 10 MLPs, with partial retirement (births 0–2) first.
ideas.projected_adjusted: If f ≤ 0.03: a0=3, util ≈10.6%, raw ×1.06–1.15, giving 2.165e-8×1.1×0.106 ≈ 2.5e-9 (×0.47, about rank 5–8). If f ≈ 0.05: raw ×1.4, giving ≈3.2e-9. If f ≥ 0.1 (the expected case): full retirement scores no better than now (≥5.8e-9). Partial retirement of births 0–2 gives util 18.8% × raw 1.1–1.4 = ×0.83–1.06. In that case there is no score gain, but it closes the learned-closure class by principle, which is material for the write-up (the $20k algorithmic prize track).

ideas.title: Zero-construction band basis: let the chain's own transport build the shared basis for old legs (a pure QR-transported Lyapunov subspace), with no Gram step, no Rayleigh–Ritz and a lazy QR. It is a free, runtime-computed stand-in for the fitted band basis
ideas.mechanism: Every old leg lies in range(T_{l<-l-a0}), because A_s = T_{l<-l-a0}·T_{l-a0<-s} and B_s = A_s U_s, and that range's energy is concentrated (Lyapunov spread; 6: top-256 = 97.5% at age 4). Transport a basis like a leg, P_{l+1} = W^T D1 P_l (with deadcut rows). Then span(P_l) = T_{l<-l-a0}·V, where V is the basis from a0 layers earlier. V depends only on W_0..W_{l-a0}, so it acts as a random probe set for T_{l<-l-a0}. The transported basis is therefore a free randomized range finder for every old leg at once, nested by construction. Legs inside span(P) stay inside exactly (A' = W^T D1 P α = P' α), so the coefficients stay fixed. QR is needed only for conditioning, every k≈3 layers, and each QR rotates the r×n coefficients. A source entering the band is projected once, P^T[A_e, B_e]. This removes exactly what closed 54: the two Gram applications on r+32 vectors (2.75 units), eigh, Rayleigh–Ritz and the per-entry rotation. Context from the column/row mechanism, measured here on dump10: the (sat,sat) block of D (α > 3 for both indices), whose every use is multiplied by w(2,1), w(3,·) ∝ φ(α) or cancels in dK21, is at most 4.6% of alive pairs at layer ≤14. The last-layer rows with negligible w(3,1) are 18%, i.e. ≤0.3% of B. The 'carries no information' mechanism has nothing big left beyond the dead side, so what remains for cost is representational.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per layer, in plain units: P transport r/n ≈ 0.31, entrant projection 2r/n ≈ 0.63, Z·P^T ≈ 0.31, QR plus rotation amortized over k=3 ≈ 0.7. That is ≈1.9 units per layer, against 4–7 for 54's entry update. The saving is ≈1.2 units per band source-layer (54's own accounting: transports + full pairings − materialisation − compressed pairing at 0.61). At a0=6, r=320 there are 55 band source-layers: 66 − 19 ≈ +47 units ≈ 4.6% of B, so util goes from 24.8% to about 20.2%. Residual time is a real constraint. k3k measured 0.413 s direct vs 0.276 s. Dropping the Gram step, eigh and Rayleigh–Ritz removes ops, but the materialisation and pairing Strassen calls stay, so the ≤0.2 s rule must be checked on the Mac.
ideas.accuracy_risk: MEDIUM. The hub leg A is coherence-sensitive: in 22, per-source SVD rank 256 from age 4 on A alone cost ×1.47. The ideal fitted band at 6:320 is +1.3%, with a cliff below r≈320. A range finder with no power iteration and no oversampling captures less energy than the fitted top-r, so it may need r = 384–448, and cost grows with r. Encouraging sign: 54's q=1 (one Gram step started from the transported basis) was within 0.2% of exact eigh, which suggests the transported subspace is already nearly right.
ideas.closest_negative: The closest is 54 (the k3k band). It was correct but cost 27.78% vs 26.62%, because its entry update ran at 4–7 units per layer against ≈1.2 saved per band source-layer. Its own notes name 'q=0 validated in torch' as the condition for reopening it. The difference here is that there is no fitting at all: the basis is a by-product of the chain's linear map, so construction is about one thin transport and the 'construction costs what it saves' mechanism does not bite. It is not 18 (Tucker core plus HOSVD refresh), and not 22 (per-source SVD).
ideas.cheap_test: First, one MLP (seconds): per layer, the energy of each old A_s, B_s outside span(P_pure), compared with the fitted band basis at r = 320 and 384. Then add a chain.py ssp mode q=-1: P transported like a leg, QR every 3 layers, first P = orth(A_e[:, :r]) of the first source to enter the band, later entrants projected with no Gram or Rayleigh–Ritz. Run 10 baked MLPs on 6:320, 6:384 and 5:384. Stop if raw > +3% at every r ≤ 384.
ideas.projected_adjusted: util ≈20.2% at raw +1.3–3% gives ×0.83–0.84, i.e. grader ≈4.5e-9. Stacked with the dead-column cut being ported (×0.936 projected) it gives ≈4.2e-9. That is not first place, and it is only worth doing if the Mac confirms residual ≤0.2 s.

verdicts.reason: This is the same mechanism §62 already measured and closed: a (t, D)-slice state moved by the exact repeated-index rule, with a cheap injector for the all-distinct part. The proposer cited only §39 and §46 and appears not to have seen §62 (dated 2026-09-28). §62 is also the 'open cloud test' the brief describes, and it has finished: (t, D) is not sufficient, a κ₃ closer must capture ≥93% of the all-distinct part, and the best O(n²) oracle captures 19.5%. title: Competitive intelligence and reasoning backwards from the leaders

ideas.title: Compact the destination rows of every leg transport (the dead-row cut currently compacts only the inner dimension). This is the compaction the leaders' telemetry shows they run.
ideas.mechanism:
k3m's transport `sw.shared(Wgv, GXv, Y[:k])` uses Wgv = Wt[:, alive_{l-1}]. It therefore compacts the inner (source) rows but still writes all n output rows at layer l. Rows of neurons below the cut at layer l are used exactly once and then gated to 0 (`d1 = d1 * mask_cur`). That single use is t_i and the star-kappa4 row for that neuron, both of which feed only its own Edgeworth mean. The alive x alive pairing, the E/L1/L2 rows and the next transport's inner dimension never read them. So transporting only the rows with alpha_l >= theta_out removes work whose sole output is a correction to near-dead means.

Size of that correction (dump10, rms of w31*t/6):
- alpha < -3.5: 7-12e-6
- alpha in [-3.5, -3.0]: 6e-5
- alpha in [-3.0, -2.5]: 1.8-2.0e-4
- for comparison, the final-layer rms error is 1.52e-4

This also requires alpha_l before the leg transport. Take Wt.C out of the fused stack and compute var = rowsum((Wt C) o Wt); the FLOPs are identical. The second C_pre product can likewise run on (alive x alive) at the same threshold.

TELEMETRY (public submission pages, 2026-09-29, 100 MLPs each):
- The leaders' per-MLP flops_used correlates with ours at r = 0.92 (J2W), 0.96 (Luna), 0.95 (#3), 0.94 (#4).
- The slopes on ours are 0.85, 1.06, 0.99 and 0.89, so the absolute sd matches ours (0.0033-0.0039 B vs 0.00355 B) at half the total.
- Solving F = V(1 - c*fbar) for our c ≈ 1.24 gives c' = 1.9-2.1 for all four leaders.
- 2-D compaction of transports and pairings predicts c ≈ 1.8-2.0; our 1-D-transport + 2-D-pairing structure predicts ≈ 1.3.
- In short, the leaders compact about 1.6x harder than we do.
ideas.cost_estimate:
The leg transport at layer l goes from (2S_l - 1)(1 - f_{l-1}) dense units to (2S_l - 1)(1 - f_{l-1})(1 - g_l), where g_l is the share of layer-l neurons with alpha < theta_out. At theta_out = -3.0 the transport-weighted g is about 0.11 (0.05 at l=6, 0.11 at l=10, 0.18 at l=15). The path leg (1 unit/layer) also drops by g, and the second C_pre product becomes (1 - g)^2 of a unit.

Construction:

ideas.title: Compute the D pairing's left factor only on kink rows. Drop the saturated rows and restore their one large-weight use (the kappa4 level) with matvecs.
ideas.mechanism:
Every consumer of row i of D (the (2,1) slice) carries a weight that vanishes on the saturated side:
- Q11 via d2_i ∝ phi(alpha)
- the C0.D diagram via w(3,p)_i ∝ alpha*phi
- DeltaK21, and hence the thin R, via c_i = d1_i(1 - d1_i) - P1_i d2_i ≈ -alpha*phi
- path leg Y via d2_i

Columns j of D (the pairing's right factor) keep weight d1_j ≈ 1 and must stay.

The one exception is the post (2,2) slice. For saturated i the Leonov-Shiryaev algebra leaves K22post_ij ∋ 2P1_j(1 - d1_j) D_ij, an O(sigma) weight. K22post is consumed only through the kappa4 level: u^T K22post u and the mean-field trace, with u = Wsq·1. That contribution is Σ_{i∈sat} u_i (D w)_i with w_j = u_j·2P1_j(1 - d1_j). It is computable exactly from the factored D = Σ L_s R_s^T by two matvecs per leg.

So the dropped rows cost nothing where it matters (level stiffness §52) and only φ-small weights elsewhere.

Saturated fractions (dump10, pairing-weighted): alpha > 3.0: 11%; > 3.5: about 7.5%. Because pairings are already compacted to alive rows, the relative saving on the pairing is 12.6% at 3.0 and 8.9% at 3.5.
ideas.cost_estimate:
The pairing at layer l goes from 2S_l x alive_l x n x alive_l to 2S_l x (alive_l - sat_l) x n x alive_l, via a rectangular paired_sum (already supported, all dims divisible by 16).

Saving: 8.9% (theta = 3.5) or 12.6% (theta = 3.0) of the ≈10.2%-of-B pairings, i.e. -0.9 or -1.3 points.

Construction: 2 matvecs per leg for the level restoration, 2S x 2n^2 flops ≈ 0.03 units/layer, plus one gather.

Util 24.84% → about 23.9% (3.5) or 23.5% (3.0).
ideas.accuracy_risk:
Weights of the dropped entries relative to their kink-neuron maxima:
- theta = 3.5: d2 at 0.2%, alpha*phi at 1.3%, c_i at 2.3%, on ≈9% of rows.
- theta = 3.0: 1.1%, 5% and 9%, on ≈13% of rows.

The errors are per-neuron, i.e. incoherent (§57), so expect < +0.5% raw at 3.5. The failure mode would be a coherent path I missed. The test measures it directly.
ideas.closest_negative: The colcut saturated side (×1.12, 1/10 MLPs) removed hub COLUMNS. Those are content of the tensor, including transported E-leg content. This idea removes output ROWS of one readout (D) and leaves the tensor, all transports and t untouched. Its only large-weight consumer is restored exactly. §57's coherence trap does not apply, because the dropped weights are per-neuron φ-tails, not a smooth fit.
ideas.cheap_test: In chain.py, after the pairing, zero D's rows with alpha_i > theta in every consumer except the kappa4 level. The level keeps the full-D value, which equals the matvec restoration. Run theta ∈ {3.5, 3.0} on the 10 baked MLPs against 2.3462e-08; kill if raw > +0.5% at 3.5. Check the level-restoration algebra at n = 128 (it must be exact to float).

verdicts.title: Compact the destination rows of every leg transport (dead rows at layer l are read only by the readout)
verdicts.already_closed_by: none. The deadcut in k3j/k3m compacts only the inner dimension. §48 and the colcut port remove hub columns. The 2026-09-25_cost §2 plan kept 't readout on all rows' as a design choice and never measured the alternative. §2 is about linearising neurons by regime, which is a different lever.
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection:
The proposer's fractions are correct. Recomputed from experiments/2026-09-27_residual/dump10.npz with deadcut −2.5 weights, the transport-weighted g is 0.086, 0.119 and 0.160 at θ_out = −3.5, −3.0 and −2.5. The final layer carries 11.8% of the transport weight.

Construction adds about 0 FLOPs. When a cut exists, k3m already runs C and the path leg in their own `sw.shared` call, so the change is a reorder (C first, var, alive_cut, then the legs with Wt[idx_out][:, idx_in]) plus row maps. Splitting the path leg out of that call adds one call per layer, about +10–40 ms of residual, which puts the grader at about 0.19–0.20 s. Keep the newest source's B in full so the star K4d stays exact; that costs about 1/15 of the saving.

Drop the C_pre alive×alive sub-idea. It is the deadC channel, which cost +0.4% MSE at −3.0 (2026-09-25_cost §2) in exchange for about 0.17 points.

Accuracy is worse than claimed. t_i is not used only once:
- It also sets K2_i, the post variance. That enters the next layer's C diagonal, which is transported in full, so it shifts every next-layer variance coherently.
- With marg=True it also sets row i's pair Wick coefficients.

Measured on dump10 at θ_out = −3.5 / −3.0 / −2.5:
- Dropping w31·t/6 at the final layer alone: raw ×1.0002 / ×1.0051 (0 of 10 MLPs better) / ×1.061.
- Mean error propagated from earlier layers (gain 2E[d1²] = 0.6–0.87 per layer): estimated +0.15% / +3% / +40%.
- Coherent next-layer variance shift per layer: 6.7e-7 / 4.5e-6 (90% same sign) / 2.3e-5. Against the §57 parabola that is ≈0 / +0.4% (±2%, depending on where the optimum sits) / +11%.

So −2.5 is dead, and −3.0 will probably breach the proposer's +0.5% kill line (estimated +1–4% raw).

Revised projection at θ_out = −3.5:
- saving 0.086 × 12.79% ≈ −1.1 points, so util goes from 24.84% to about 23.7% (×0.956)
- raw ×1.002, so the adjusted factor is about ×0.958
- alone: ≈5.16e-9
- on top of the matched colcut port (≈4.95e-9): ≈4.75e-9

At −3.0, only if the test shows raw ≤ +1%: ≈5.1e-9.
verdicts.reason:
This is a genuine new axis: the destination dimension of the shipped cut. It is fair accounting under §5.5 (the computation genuinely gets smaller) and uses no rival code.

The FLOP saving is exact and needs no new basis, so the §54–§59 construction trap does not apply.

The proposer's premise ('feeds only its own Edgeworth mean') is incomplete: the K2 and marg channels exist. That makes −3.0 doubtful and −2.5 dead. At −3.5 the lever is worth about 4% for about 0.2% raw risk, just above the grader's 2–3% resolution.

verdicts.title: Compute the D pairing's left factor only on kink rows; drop saturated rows and restore their κ4-level contribution by matvecs
verdicts.already_closed_by: none. The nearest measurement is today's naive saturated-row scan (experiments/2026-09-29_satrow/scan_n10.log), which zeroed saturated D rows everywhere, including the κ4 level. That is not a closure. The colcut saturated side (×1.12) cut a different object: hub columns carrying transported content.
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection:
Savings, verified from dump10: the pairing-weighted relative saving is 12.6% at θ = 3.0 and 8.9% at θ = 3.5, i.e. −1.34 and −0.95 points of B. The satrow scan modelled only −0.84 points at 3.0 because it used the unweighted layer mean (7.9%).

Algebra, verified: in K22o both orientations of D_ij with i saturated carry 2P1_j·d1_i·(1−d1_j). The level restoration is therefore exactly 2 Σ_{i∈sat} u_i (D w)_i with w_j = 2u_j·P1_j·(1−d1_j). That costs O(S n²), about 0.03 units per layer. The K21 path cancels consistently: the pass-through subtraction d1_i²·d1_j·D_ij sees the same cut D, leaving only c_i.

What the naive scan measured (level not restored):
- at 3.0: raw ×1.0094, 6 of 10 MLPs better, per-MLP ×0.84 to ×1.35
- at 2.5: ×1.34, all 10 worse

Projection with restoration:
- θ = 3.0: util ×0.946 × raw ≈1.003–1.01 = ×0.95–0.955, i.e. ≈5.14e-9 alone
- θ = 3.5: ×0.962 × ≈1.002, i.e. ≈5.2e-9
- stacked on the first idea (−3.5) and colcut: ≈4.55e-9
verdicts.reason:
The mechanism is sound and the construction is correctly priced and negligible.

The naive scan's large per-MLP swings are what an unrestored, stiff κ4 level would produce (§52 stiffness: ×2.8 per 5%). The level weight 2P1_j(1−d1_j) does not decay with how saturated row i is. This idea restores exactly that channel.

Even the naive cut at 3.0 nets about ×0.955 once the saving is weighted correctly, but with only 6 of 10 MLPs better, which fails the breadth rule.

Remaining risk: c_i ≈ −αφ is about 12% of its kink maximum at 3.0 and about 3% at 3.5. It feeds R's rank-24 randomized sketch (which is non-monotone) and births that persist (a soft channel with no √n discount, §58). That could keep the spread even after restoration.

Test: add a level-restored satrow switch at 3.0, 3.25 and 3.5 on 10 MLPs. Accept only if at least 9 of 10 are better on adjusted and the per-MLP spread collapses; otherwise close it.

verdicts.title: Spend freed wall on Strassen L5 for the D pairings only (full L5 later)
verdicts.already_closed_by: §56 (Strassen L5: the meter pays ×0.9165 but the level is memory-bandwidth bound; wall ×1.95 and RSS 7.81 GB). A pairing-only L5 is the same lever with the same mechanism at a smaller dose.
verdicts.revised_cost_and_projection:
Wall:
- Pairings are about 42% of Strassen work (10.62 of about 25.4 billed points). Doubling that part's wall gives about ×1.40 in total.
- On k3m the worst grader MLP goes from 75.3 s to about 105 s.
- After the first idea at −3.5 plus the third idea plus colcut, work falls about 10–12%, not 16% (−3.0 and −2.5 are not viable). That gives about 93 s.
- The grader's worst-MLP wall moved between 63.7 and 75.3 s across submissions with identical FLOPs (±18%), so the true worst case could reach about 110 s against the 120 s cap.

RSS:
- The workspace allocates the L5 region whatever calls use it. At chunk 16 that is +2.2 GB, about 7.8 GB total as in §56.
- At chunk 8 it is +1.1 GB, about 6.6 GB total, not the 4.5–5.5 GB claimed.
- Chunk 8 costs residual (§49; §56 probe: 0.364 s).

Billing:
- L5 on compacted n' ≈ 800 needs dimensions divisible by 32 (more padding) and leaves of about 25–26. The billing gain is therefore below ×0.9165.
- Saving ≈ 9.3% × 0.08 ≈ −0.7 points of B, i.e. about ×0.965 on a base near 21%.
verdicts.reason:
This does not escape §56's mechanism; it spends wall headroom that exists only if two other unbuilt levers land, and even then it is thin.

The prize is about 3%, at the grader's resolution. The downside is catastrophic: a single wall or RSS breach on the private re-evaluation zeroes that MLP (MSE about 0.9 at multiplier 1.0). That adds about 9e-3 to the 100-MLP mean and destroys the entry.

The RSS and residual construction costs are under-priced.

Reopen only as a measured decision on wall time, once a stacked build's worst grader MLP is at or below about 60 s.
